1
呂大防
Lü Dafang
2
呂大防，字微仲，其先汲郡人。 祖通，太常博士。 父賁，比部郎中。 通葬京兆藍田，遂家焉。 大防進士及第，調馮翊主簿、永壽令。 縣無井，遠汲於澗，大防行近境，得二泉，欲導而入縣，地勢高下，眾疑無成理。 大防用《考工》水地置泉之法以準之，不旬日，果疏為渠，民賴之，號曰「呂公泉」。
Lü Dafang, whose courtesy name was Weizhong, came from a family originally of Ji Commandery. His grandfather Tong served as Erudite of the Imperial Diener. His father Ben held the post of Director in the Ministry of Revenue. When Tong died he was buried at Lantian in Jingzhao, and the family made their home there. Dafang passed the jinshi examinations and was posted as main clerk of Fengyi and magistrate of Yongshou. The county had no wells and had to draw water from distant ravines. When Dafang toured the nearby countryside he found two springs and planned to channel them into the seat, but the terrain was uneven and people doubted the project could work. Dafang surveyed the site by the Kaogongji's methods for siting springs from terrain and water, and within ten days a channel was cut as planned. The people depended on it and called it "Lord Lü's Spring."
3
遷著作佐郎、知青城縣。 故時，圭田粟入以大斗，而出以公斗，獲利三倍，民雖病不敢訴。 大防始均出納以平其直，事轉聞，詔立法禁，命一路悉輸租於官概給之。 青城外控汶川，與敵相接。 大防據要置邏，密為之防，禁山之樵採，以嚴障蔽。 韓絳鎮蜀，稱其有王佐才。 入權鹽鐵判官。
He was promoted to assistant editor in the Palace Library and appointed magistrate of Qingcheng. Under the old practice, grain from ceremonial fields was collected with the large bushel but disbursed with the standard bushel, tripling the profit. The people suffered but dared not protest. Dafang first balanced collections and disbursements to even out the price. When word reached the court, an edict outlawed the practice and required the whole circuit to pay rent to the government, which would then issue grain by the standard measure. Beyond Qingcheng lay Wenchuan, on the frontier where the enemy could be met. Dafang held strategic points and established courier posts, quietly strengthening defenses and banning logging in the mountains to keep the border screen intact. When Han Jiang was military commissioner of Shu, he praised Dafang as having the makings of a chief minister. He was summoned to the capital to serve as acting commissioner of the Salt and Iron Monopoly.
4
英宗即位，改太常博士。 御史闕，內出大防與范純仁姓名，命為監察御史裏行。 首言：「紀綱賞罰，未厭四方之望者有五：進用大臣而權不歸上； 大臣疲老而不得時退； 外國驕蹇而不擇將帥； 議論之臣裨益闕失，而大臣沮之； 疆場左右之臣，有敗事而被賞、舉職而獲罪者。 」又言：「富弼病足請解機務，章十餘上而不納； 張昪年幾八十，聰明已耗，哀乞骸骨而不從； 吳奎有三年之喪，以其子召之者再，遣使召之者又再； 程戡辭老不能守邊，恐死塞上，免以屍柩還家為請，亦不許。 陛下欲盡君臣之分，使病者得休，喪者得終，老者得盡其餘年，則進退盡禮，亦何必過為虛飾，使四人之誠，不得自達邪？」
When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, Dafang was reassigned as erudite of the Imperial Diener. When a censor's post fell vacant, the palace released the names of Dafang and Fan Chunren and appointed them supervising censors with acting status. In his opening memorial he said: "In discipline and in rewards and punishments, five things still fall short of what the realm expects: great ministers are advanced while authority does not return to the throne; great ministers, worn out with age, cannot step down when they should; foreign powers grow arrogant while commanders are not chosen with care; censors who would remedy faults are blocked by the great ministers; and on the frontiers there are men who fail yet are rewarded and men who do their duty yet are punished." " He went on: "Fu Bi, afflicted in the feet, asked to leave state affairs; he sent more than ten memorials without success; Zhang Bian is nearly eighty and his faculties are spent, yet his plea to retire is refused; Wu Kui is in mourning for his father and has been summoned twice through his son and twice again by imperial envoys; Cheng Kan begs off on account of age, saying he cannot hold the border and fears dying on campaign, asking only the grace of not having to bring his coffin home from the frontier—yet this too is denied. If Your Majesty wishes to honor the bond between ruler and minister—so the sick may rest, the bereaved may mourn, and the aged may live out their years—then let advance and withdrawal follow proper ritual. Why insist on empty ceremony that keeps these four men's sincerity from reaching you?"
5
是歲，京師大水，大防曰：「雨水之患，至入宮城廬舍，殺人害物，此陰陽之沴也。 」即陳八事，曰：主威不立、臣權太盛、邪議干正、私恩害公、遼夏連謀、盜賊恣行、群情失職、刑罰失平。 會執政議濮王稱考，大防上言：「先帝起陛下為皇子，館於宮中，憑几之命，緒言在耳，皇天后土，實知所託。 設使先帝萬壽，陛下猶為皇子，則安懿之稱伯，於理不疑。 豈可生以為子，沒而背之哉？ 夫人君臨御之始，宜有至公大義厭服天下，以結其心。 今大臣首欲加王以非正之號，使陛下顧私恩而違公義，非所以結天下之心也。 」章累十數上，出知休寧縣。
That year the capital was inundated. Dafang said: "When rain and flood enter the palace city and common houses, killing people and destroying property, this is a disorder of yin and yang." " He then listed eight ills: the throne's authority is not firm; ministers are too powerful; wicked counsel overrides right policy; private favor injures the public good; Liao and Xia plot together; bandits roam unchecked; public morale is out of joint; and punishments are uneven. When the chief ministers debated granting the Prince of Pu the title Imperial Father, Dafang memorialized: "The late emperor raised Your Majesty as crown prince and housed you in the palace. The charge spoken at his couch still rings in our ears; Heaven and Earth know whom he truly entrusted." Had the late emperor lived on and Your Majesty remained crown prince, calling Prince An Yi "uncle" would have been entirely proper. How can he be made a son in life and repudiated in death? At the start of a reign the ruler should win the realm with utmost fairness and public duty, binding hearts to the throne. Now the chief ministers would first give the prince an improper title, leading Your Majesty to favor private feeling over public duty. That is no way to win the realm's hearts. " After more than ten such memorials he was transferred out to serve as magistrate of Xiuning.
6
神宗立，通判淄州。 熙寧元年，知泗州，為河北轉運副使。 召直舍人院。 韓絳宣撫陝西，命為判官，又兼河東宣撫判官，除知制誥。 四年，知廷州。 大防、昉欲城河外荒堆砦，眾謂不可守，大防留戍兵修堡障，有不從者斬以徇。 會環慶兵亂，絳坐黜，大防亦落知制誥，以太常博士知臨江軍。
When Emperor Shenzong came to the throne, Dafang was appointed vice-prefect of Zizhou. In the first year of Xining he became prefect of Sizhou and vice transport commissioner of Hebei. He was recalled to duty in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies. When Han Jiang was pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, Dafang served as his aide and also as aide to the Hedong pacification commissioner, and was appointed drafter of edicts. In the fourth year he was appointed prefect of Yanzhou. Dafang and Fang wanted to wall desolate beacon forts beyond the river, though many said they could not be held. Dafang left garrison troops to build fortifications and executed any who refused, as an example. When the Huanqing garrison mutinied, Han Jiang was dismissed and Dafang was stripped of his post as drafter of edicts, becoming erudite of the Imperial Diener while governing Linjiang.
7
數月，徙知華州。 華嶽摧，自山屬渭河，被害者眾。 大防奏疏，援經質史，以驗時事。 其略曰：「『畏天之威，於時保之。 』先王所以興也； 『我生不有命在天』，後王所以壞也。 《書》云：『惟先格王，正厥事。 』願仰承天威，俯酌時變，為社稷至計。 」除龍圖閣待制、知秦州。 元豐初，徙永興。 神宗以彗星求言，大防陳三說九宜：曰治本、曰緩末、曰納言。 養民、教士、重穀，治本之宜三也； 治邊、治兵，緩末之宜二也； 廣受言之路，寬侵官之罰，恕誹謗之罪，容異同之論，此納言之宜四也。 累數千言。 時用兵西夏，調度百出，有不便者輒上聞，務在寬民。 及兵罷，民力比他路為饒，供億軍須亦無乏絕。 進直學士。 居數年，知成都府。
Several months later he was transferred to Huazhou as prefect. Mount Hua collapsed, debris running from the mountain down to the Wei River, and many were killed or injured. Dafang memorialized the throne, citing the classics and weighing history against present events. In summary he wrote: "'Revere Heaven's majesty and in due season preserve your rule'— that is how the ancient kings rose; 'My life rests not with myself but with Heaven's mandate'—that is how later kings fell. The Documents says: 'Only by first understanding the king can his affairs be set right.' ' I pray Your Majesty will look up to Heaven's majesty and look down to the changes of the age, and take the course that best secures the realm." " He was appointed academician-on-waiting at the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Qinzhou. Early in Yuanfeng he was transferred to Yongxing. When a comet prompted Emperor Shenzong to seek counsel, Dafang offered three doctrines and nine measures: strengthen the root, ease the branches, and welcome frank speech. Nourish the people, educate scholars, and value grain—these three strengthen the root; govern the frontier and govern the army—these two ease the branches; widen the channels for counsel, lighten penalties for overstepping office, pardon charges of slander, and tolerate dissent—these four welcome frank speech. The memorial ran to several thousand words. While the court campaigned against Western Xia, levies multiplied. Whenever a measure burdened the people he reported it at once, always seeking to lighten their load. When the war ended, his circuit's people were better off than elsewhere, yet military supplies never ran short. He was promoted to Hanlin academician. After several years he was appointed prefect of Chengdu.
8
哲宗即位，召為翰林學士、權開封府。 有僧誑民取財，因訟至廷下。 驗治得情，命抱具獄，即其所杖之，他挾奸者皆遁去。 館伴契丹使，其使黠，語頗及朝廷，大防密擿其隱事，詰之曰：「北朝試進士《至心獨運賦》，不知此題於書何出？ 」使錯遌不能對，自是不敢復出嫚詞。
When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Dafang was recalled as Hanlin academician and acting prefect of Kaifeng. A monk who swindled the people was brought to court in a lawsuit. Once the facts were proved, Dafang had the man carry the punishment gear to the scene of his crime and beaten there on the spot. Other swindlers fled. While hosting a Khitan envoy, a clever man who often alluded to court affairs, Dafang quietly uncovered a compromising detail and asked him: "Your court's recent jinshi examination used the topic 'With Utmost Sincerity the Heart Moves Alone'—from which classic does that phrase come?" " The envoy was abashed and could not reply, and never again dared speak insolently.
9
遷吏部尚書。 夏使來，詔訪以待遇之計，且曰：「向者所得邊地，雖建立城堡，終慮孤絕難保。 棄之則弱國，守之又有後悔，為當奈何？ 」大防言：「夏本無能為，然屢遣使而不布誠款者，蓋料我急於議和耳。 今使者到闕，宜令押伴臣僚，扣其不賀登極，以觀厥意，足以測情偽矣。 新收疆土，議者多言可棄，此慮之不熟也。 至於守御之策，惟擇將帥為先。 太祖用姚內斌、董遵誨守環、慶，西人不敢入侵。 昔以二州之力，禦敵而有餘； 今以九州之大，奉邊而不足。 由是言之，在於得人而已。 」元祐元年，拜尚書右丞，進中書侍郎，封汲郡公。 西方息兵，青唐羌以為中國怯，使大將鬼章青宜結犯邊。 大防命洮州諸將乘間致討，生擒之。
He was promoted to minister of personnel. When a Western Xia envoy arrived, the emperor asked his advice on how to treat them, saying: "The frontier lands we recently gained have fortresses, yet we fear they are too isolated to hold. To abandon them weakens the state, yet to hold them may bring regret—what should we do?" " Dafang replied: "The Xia are not truly formidable, yet they send envoys again and again without sincere overtures because they assume we are eager for peace. Now that the envoy is at court, let the escorting officials press him on why he did not congratulate Your Majesty's accession. His response will reveal his true intentions. As for the newly taken lands, many advisers say we should abandon them—but that judgment is immature. For defense, the first priority is choosing the right commanders. Taizu posted Yao Neibin and Dong Zunhui at Huan and Qing, and the western peoples dared not invade. Once two prefectures sufficed to repel the enemy with strength to spare; now with the resources of the whole realm, the frontier still seems underfed. The difference, in short, is whether we have the right men. " In the first year of Yuanyou he became right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, then vice director of the Secretariat, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji. When fighting in the west subsided, the Qingtang Qiang judged China timid and sent the general Guizhang Qingyijie to raid the frontier. Dafang ordered the generals of Taozhou to strike when opportunity allowed and they took him alive.
10
三年，呂公著告老，宣仁后欲留之京師。 手札密訪至於四五，超拜大防尚書左僕射兼門下侍郎，提舉修《神宗實錄》。 大防見哲宗年益壯，日以進學為急，請敕講讀官取仁宗邇英御書解釋上之，置於座右。 又摭乾興以來四十一事足以為勸戒者，分上下篇，標曰《仁祖聖學》，使人主有欣慕不足之意。
In the third year Lü Gongzhu sought to retire, and Empress Dowager Xuanren wished to keep him in the capital. She consulted him privately by letter four or five times, then promoted Dafang to left grand master of the palace and vice director of the Chancellery, putting him in charge of compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong. Seeing Zhezong grow older, Dafang pressed daily for his education and asked that lecture officials submit Emperor Renzong's annotated Yiying lectures for placement at the emperor's side. He also compiled forty-one instructive episodes since Qianxing into upper and lower volumes titled The Sagely Learning of Emperor Ren, meant to inspire the ruler with lasting admiration.
11
哲宗御邇英閣，召宰執、講讀官讀《寶訓》，至「漢武帝籍南山提封為上林苑，仁宗曰：『山澤之利當與眾共之，何用此也。 』丁度曰：『臣事陛下二十年，每奉德音，未始不及於憂勤，此蓋祖宗家法爾。 』」大防因推廣祖宗家法以進，曰：「自三代以後，唯本朝百二十年中外無事，蓋由祖宗所立家法最善，臣請舉其略。 自古人主事母后，朝見有時，如漢武帝五日一朝長樂宮； 祖宗以來事母后，皆朝夕見，此事親之法也。 前代大長公主用臣妾之禮； 本朝必先致恭，仁宗以姪事姑之禮見獻穆大長公主，此事長之法也。 前代宮闈多不肅，宮人或與廷臣相見，唐入閣圖有昭容位； 本朝宮禁嚴密，內外整肅，此治內之法也。 前代外戚多預政事，常致敗亂； 本朝母后之族皆不預，此待外戚之法也。 前代宮室多尚華侈； 本朝宮殿止用赤白，此尚儉之法也。 前代人君雖在宮禁，出輿入輦； 祖宗皆步自內庭，出御後殿，豈乏人力哉？ 亦欲涉歷廣庭，稍冒寒暑，此勤身之法也。 前代人主，在禁中冠服苟簡； 祖宗以來，燕居必以禮，竊聞陛下昨郊禮畢，具禮謝太皇太后，此尚禮之法也。 前代多深於用刑，大者誅戮，小者遠竄； 惟本朝用法最輕，臣下有罪，止於罷黜，此寬仁之法也。 至於虛己納諫，不好畋獵，不尚玩好，不用玉器，不貴異味，此皆祖宗家法，所以致太平者。 陛下不須遠法前代，但盡行家法，足以為天下。 」哲宗甚然之。
At the Yiying Pavilion Zhezong summoned the chief ministers and lecture officials to read the Precious Instructions. They came to the passage where Emperor Wu of Han seized the southern hills for the Shanglin Park and Emperor Renzong said: "The bounty of hills and marshes should be shared with the people—what need is there for this?" ' Ding Du replied: "In twenty years serving Your Majesty, every gracious word I have heard has spoken of anxious diligence for the realm—such is our ancestors' household rule."' " Dafang then expanded on the ancestral household rules, saying: "Since antiquity only our dynasty has enjoyed roughly 120 years largely free of turmoil within and without, because the rules our ancestors established are the finest. I beg leave to summarize them. Ancient rulers visited their empress mothers on a fixed schedule—Emperor Wu of Han, for example, attended the Everlasting Joy Palace once every five days; but our house has always visited empress mothers morning and evening. That is how we honor our kin. Earlier dynasties treated elder imperial princesses with the ceremony owed to ministers and concubines; our house always shows respect first—Emperor Renzong received the Great Elder Princess Xianmu with a nephew's courtesy toward his aunt. That is how we honor our elders. In earlier times the inner palace was often lax and palace women might meet court officials—the Tang painting of entering the hall even marks a place for palace ladies; our palace precincts are strict and discipline is maintained within and without. That is how we govern the inner court. In former times consort kin often meddled in politics and brought ruin; in our house the empress mother's kin never hold office. That is how we treat consort relatives. Earlier palaces prized lavish ornament; our palaces use only red and white. That is how we value frugality. Earlier rulers, even within the palace, rode out in carriages and palanquins; our ancestors walked from the inner court to the rear hall—was it for lack of attendants? No—they wished to cross the broad courtyards and bear a little heat and cold. That is how they kept their bodies disciplined. Earlier rulers dressed casually in the palace precincts; Since our ancestors, even in private life we observe proper ceremony. I have heard that after yesterday's suburban sacrifice Your Majesty performed full rites to thank the Grand Empress Dowager. That is how we honor ritual propriety. Earlier dynasties punished harshly—the greatest offenders were executed and lesser ones were banished far away; Our house alone applies the law most leniently. When officials err, dismissal is the limit. That is how we practice generous clemency. Emptying oneself to accept remonstrance, shunning the hunt, spurning trifles, eschewing jade ware, and disdaining exotic delicacies—all these ancestral family laws are what brought about great peace. Your Majesty need not look to former ages for models. Simply follow the family laws fully, and that is enough to govern the realm. Emperor Zhezong strongly approved.
12
大防樸厚惷直，不植黨朋，與范純仁並位，同心戮力，以相王室。 立朝挺挺，進退百官，不可干以私，不市恩嫁怨以邀聲譽，凡八年，始終如一。
Dafang was plainspoken, honest, and upright, and kept no faction of his own. Sharing office with Fan Chunren, the two worked in concert to serve the throne. In court he held himself erect. No one could sway his decisions on appointing or removing officials through private appeals, nor did he trade favors or shift blame to win renown. For eight years he was unwavering.
13
懇乞避位，宣仁后曰：「上方富於春秋，公未可即去，少須歲月，吾亦就東朝矣。 」未果而后崩。 為山陵使，覆命以觀文殿大學士、左光祿大夫知潁昌府。 尋改永興軍，使便其鄉社。 入辭，哲宗勞慰甚渥，曰：「卿暫歸故鄉，行即召矣。 」未幾，左正言上官均論其隳壞役法，右正言張商英、御史周秩、劉拯相繼攻之，奪學士，知隨州，貶秘書監，分司南京，居郢州。 言者又以修《神宗實錄》直書其事為誣詆，徙安州。
He earnestly asked to step down. Empress Dowager Xuanren said, "The emperor is still young. You, sir, cannot leave yet. Wait a few months—I too shall retire to the Eastern Palace." Before that could happen, the empress dowager died. As commissioner for the imperial tomb, he reported back and was appointed grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, left grand master of splendid happiness, and prefect of Yingchang. He was soon transferred to Yongxing Circuit to be nearer his home. When he came to take leave, Emperor Zhezong comforted him warmly and said, "Return home for a time—you will soon be summoned again." Before long Left Rectifier Shangguan Jun accused him of undermining the corvée law. Right Rectifier Zhang Shangying and Censors Zhou Zhi and Liu Zheng attacked him in turn. He lost his academician title, was posted as prefect of Suizhou, demoted to supervisor of the Secretariat with duties at the Southern Capital branch, and lived at Yingzhou. Critics also charged that in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong he had written events plainly, which they called slander, and he was moved to Anzhou.
14
兄大忠自渭入對，哲宗詢大防安否，且曰：「執政欲遷諸嶺南，朕獨令處安陸，為朕寄聲問之。 大防樸直，為人所賣，三二年可復相見也。 」大忠泄其語於章惇，惇懼，繩之愈力。 紹聖四年，遂貶舒州團練副使，安置循州。 至虔州信豐而病，語其子景山曰：「吾不復南矣！ 吾死汝歸，呂氏尚有遺種。 」遂薨，年七十一。 大忠請歸葬，許之。
His elder brother Dazhong came from Weizhou for audience. Emperor Zhezong asked after Dafang's health and said, "The chief ministers wanted to banish them all south of the mountains. I alone had him placed at Anlu. Convey my greetings to him for me." Dafang is straightforward and has been sold out by others. In two or three years you may see each other again. Dazhong repeated this to Zhang Dun. Dun, alarmed, pressed the case against Dafang even harder. In the fourth year of Shaosheng he was demoted to assistant commissioner of militia training for Shuzhou and exiled to Xunzhou. At Xinfeng in Qianzhou he fell ill and told his son Jingshan, "I will go no farther south!" When I die, you return home. The Lü line will not die out. He died at seventy-one. Dazhong petitioned for burial in their home region and permission was granted.
15
大防身長七尺，眉目秀發，聲音如鐘。 自少持重，無嗜好，過市不左右游目，燕居如對賓客。 每朝會，威儀翼如，神宗常目送之。 與大忠及弟大臨同居，相切磋論道考禮，冠昏喪祭，一本於古，關中言《禮》學者推呂氏。 嘗為《鄉約》曰：「凡同約者，德業相勸，過失相規，禮俗相交，患難相恤，有善則書於籍，有過若違約者亦書之，三犯而行罰，不悛者絕之。」
Dafang stood seven chi tall, with handsome features and luxuriant hair, and a voice resonant as a bell. From youth he was solemn and without indulgence. He never glanced about in the marketplace, and even in private he conducted himself as if before guests. At every court assembly his bearing was dignified and precise. Emperor Shenzong often followed him with his gaze as he departed. He lived with Dazhong and his younger brother Dalin, studying the Way and ritual together. Capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice in their household all followed ancient models, and in Guanzhong students of ritual pointed to the Lüs as models. He once drafted a Village Covenant: "All members shall encourage one another in virtue and learning, admonish one another over faults, join in ritual and custom, and help one another in hardship. Good deeds are recorded; faults and violations are recorded too. After three offenses there is punishment; the unreformed are expelled."
16
徽宗即位，復其官。 高宗紹興初，又復大學士，贈太師、宣國公，諡曰「正愍」。
When Emperor Huizong came to the throne, Dafang's offices were restored. Early in the Shaoxing reign Emperor Gaozong restored his grand academician title, posthumously enfeoffed him as grand preceptor and Duke of Xuan, and gave him the posthumous title Zhengmin.
17
兄大忠
Elder Brother: Dazhong
18
大忠，字進伯。 登第，為華陰尉、晉城令。 韓絳宣撫陝西，以大忠提舉永興路義勇。 改秘書丞，檢詳樞密院吏、兵房文字。 令條義勇利害。 大忠言：「養兵猥眾，國用日屈，漢之屯田，唐之府兵，善法也。 弓箭手近於屯田，義勇近於府兵，擇用一焉，兵屯可省矣。 」為簽書定國軍判官。
Dazhong, courtesy name Jinbo. He passed the examinations and served as assistant magistrate of Huayin and magistrate of Jincheng. When Han Jiang served as commissioner to pacify Shaanxi, he appointed Dazhong to oversee the volunteer forces of Yongxing Circuit. He was transferred to secretary of the Secretariat and assigned to examine documents in the personnel and military sections of the Bureau of Military Affairs. He was ordered to itemize the pros and cons of the volunteer force system. Dazhong said, "The army has grown wastefully large and state finances dwindle by the day. Han garrison farming and Tang militia levies were sound models." Archer-soldiers resemble garrison farming and volunteer forces resemble militia levies. Adopt one of these models and garrison costs can be cut. He was appointed signing clerk and military administrator of Dingguo Army.
19
熙寧中，王安石議遣使諸道，立緣邊封溝，大忠與范育被命，俱辭行。 大忠陳五不可，以為懷撫外國，恩信不洽，必致生患。 罷不遣。 令與劉忱使契丹，議代北地，會遭父喪。 起復，知代州。 契丹使蕭素、梁潁至代，設次，據主席，大忠與之爭，乃移次於長城北。 換西上閤門使、知石州。 大忠數與素、潁會，凡議，屢以理折之，素、潁稍屈。 已而復使蕭禧來求代北地，神宗召執政與大忠、忱議，將從其請。 大忠曰：「彼遣一使來，即與地五百里，若使魏王英弼來求關南，則何如？ 」神宗曰：「卿是何言也。 」對曰：「陛下既以臣言為不然，恐不可啟其漸。 」忱曰：「大忠之言，社稷大計，願陛下熟思之。 」執政知不可奪，議卒不決，罷忱還三司，大忠亦終喪制。 其後竟以分水嶺為界焉。
During the Xining reforms Wang Anshi proposed sending envoys to the circuits to dig border demarcation trenches along the frontier. Dazhong and Fan Yu received the orders but both declined the mission. Dazhong set out five reasons against the plan, arguing that if grace and trust were not established in dealing with foreign peoples, trouble would follow. The plan was dropped and the envoys were not sent. He was ordered to join Liu Chen on a mission to the Khitan to negotiate over lands north of Dai, but his father died before he could depart. Called back from mourning, he was appointed prefect of Daizhou. Khitan envoys Xiao Su and Liang Ying arrived at Daizhou. When the reception tent was set up they claimed the seat of honor. Dazhong protested and the tent was moved beyond the Great Wall. He was appointed commissioner of the Western Upper Gate and prefect of Shizhou. Dazhong met repeatedly with Xiao Su and Liang Ying. In every round of talks he wore them down with reason, and they gradually gave ground. Later Xiao Xi was sent again to demand lands north of Dai. Emperor Shenzong summoned the chief ministers along with Dazhong and Liu Chen to consult, and was inclined to accede. Dazhong said, "They send one envoy and we hand over five hundred li of territory. What if the Wei king Yingbi came demanding Guannan?" Emperor Shenzong said, "What sort of talk is that?" He replied, "If Your Majesty rejects what I say, I fear we must not open the door to incremental demands." Liu Chen said, "Dazhong speaks for the security of the realm. I urge Your Majesty to weigh his words carefully." The chief ministers saw they could not prevail. The deliberations ended unresolved. Liu Chen was sent back to the Three Departments and Dazhong completed his mourning observances. In the end the frontier was fixed at Watershed Ridge.
20
元豐中，為河北轉運判官，言：「古者理財，視天下猶一家。 朝廷者家，外計者兄弟，居雖異而財無不同。 今有司惟知出納之名，有餘不足，未嘗以實告上。 故有餘則取之，不足莫之與，甚大患也。 」乃上生財、養民十二事。 徙提點淮西刑獄。 時河決，飛蝗為災，大忠入對，極論之，詔歸故官。
During the Yuanfeng era, as transport commissioner for Hebei, he said, "In antiquity fiscal administration treated the realm as one household." The court is the household and the outer circuits are like brothers. They may dwell apart, but their wealth is shared. Today officials know only receipts and disbursements by name. Surplus and shortage are never reported honestly to the throne. Where there is surplus they take; where there is shortage none is supplied. That is a grave evil. He then submitted twelve proposals for generating revenue and nourishing the people. He was transferred to intendant of judicial affairs for Huai West. The Yellow River had breached its banks and locusts ravaged the land. Dazhong had audience with the emperor and spoke at length on both crises. An edict restored him to his former post.
21
元祐初，歷工部郎中、陝西轉運副使、知陝州，以直龍圖閣知秦州，進寶文閣待制。 夏人自犯麟府、環慶後，遂絕歲賜，欲遣使謝罪，神宗將許之。 大忠言：「夏人強則縱，困則服，今陽為恭順，實懼討伐。 宜且命邊臣詰其所以來之辭，若惟請是從，彼將有以窺我矣。」
Early in Yuanyou he served successively as director in the Ministry of Works, deputy transport commissioner for Shaanxi, and prefect of Shanzhou; then, as direct associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall, prefect of Qinzhou, and was promoted to appointed draft master of the Hall for Treasuring Culture. After the Tangut attacks on Lin, Fu, Huan, and Qing, they suspended the annual tribute payments and wished to send envoys to apologize. Emperor Shenzong was inclined to accept. Dazhong said, "When the Tangut are strong we indulge them; when they are cornered they submit. Now they pretend deference but really fear punishment." Your Majesty should first have frontier officials challenge the stated reasons for their mission. If we simply grant every request, they will learn to test us."
22
時郡糴民粟，豪家因之制操縱之柄。 大忠選僚寀自旦入倉，雖斗升亦受，不使有所壅閼。 民喜，爭運粟於倉，負錢而去，得百餘萬斛。
The prefecture was buying grain from the people, and powerful families seized control of the market. Dazhong picked officials to staff the granary from dawn, accepting every measure down to the smallest so nothing would be turned away. The people rejoiced and rushed grain to the granary. They took payment and left. More than a million hu were collected.
23
馬涓以進士舉首入幕府，自稱狀元。 大忠謂曰：「狀元云者，及第未除官之稱也，既為判官則不可。 今科舉之習既無用，修身為己之學，不可不勉。 」又教以臨政治民之要，涓自以為得師焉。 謝良佐教授州學，大忠每過之，聽講《論語》，必正襟斂容曰：「聖人言行在焉，吾不敢不肅。」
Ma Juan, who had placed first on the jinshi list, joined the staff and styled himself zhuangyuan. Dazhong told him, "Zhuangyuan is what one is called between passing the examinations and receiving an appointment. As a staff judge you cannot use it." The habits of the examination halls are worthless now. You must devote yourself to learning that cultivates the self." He also taught him the essentials of governance. Juan felt he had found a true teacher. Xie Liangzuo taught at the prefectural school. Whenever Dazhong stopped to hear him lecture on the Analects, he would sit up straight and say, "The sage's words and conduct are present here. I dare not be irreverent."
24
嘗獻曰：「夏人戍守之外，戰士不過十萬，吾三路之眾，足以當之矣。 彼屢犯王略，一不與校，臣竊羞之。 」紹聖二年，加寶文閣直學士、知渭州，付以秦、渭之事，奏言：「關、陝民力未裕，士氣沮喪，非假之歲月，未易枝梧。 」因請以職事對。 大抵欲以計徐取橫山，自汝遮殘井迤邐進築，不求近功。
He once submitted a memorial: "Apart from garrison troops, the Tangut field no more than one hundred thousand fighters. Our forces in the three circuits are enough to meet them." They have violated our territory again and again without our answering once. I am ashamed of this." In the second year of Shaosheng he was made direct academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and prefect of Weizhou, with authority over Qin and Wei. He submitted: "In Guan and Shaanxi the people are not yet recovered and morale is low. Without time, the frontier cannot be held." He asked to report on his duties in a special audience. In general he planned to take Hengshan gradually, advancing fortifications step by step from Ruzhe and Canjing without seeking quick success.
25
既而鐘傅城安西，王文郁亦用事，章惇、曾布主之，大忠議不合； 又乞以所進職為大防量移，惇、布陳其所言與元祐時異，徙知同州，旋降待制致仕。 卒，詔復學士官，佐其葬。
Soon Zhong Fu fortified Anxi and Wang Wenyü gained influence, backed by Zhang Dun and Zeng Bu. Dazhong's views differed. He also asked that the office he had just received be used to secure a less harsh transfer for Dafang. Zhang Dun and Zeng Bu cited his statements as inconsistent with his Yuanyou positions. He was moved to Tongzhou, then demoted from draft master and retired. When he died, an edict restored his academician title and provided assistance for his burial.
26
弟大鈞
Younger Brother: Dajun
27
大鈞，字和叔。 父蕡，六子，其五登科，大鈞第三子也。 中乙科，調秦州右司理參軍，監延州折博務。 改光祿寺丞、知三原縣。 請代蕡入蜀，移巴西縣。 蕡致仕，大鈞亦移疾不行。
Dajun, courtesy name Heshu. His father Ben had six sons, five of whom passed the examinations. Dajun was the third son. He passed in the second examination category and was assigned judicial assistant of the right section at Qinzhou and superintendent of the tea-and-horse trade at Yanzhou. He was promoted to assistant director of the Office of Imperial Entertainments and appointed magistrate of Sanyuan County. He asked to take his father's place on a posting into Shu and was transferred to Baxi County. When Ben retired, Dajun also pleaded illness and declined to serve.
28
韓絳宣撫陝西、河東，辟書寫機密文字。 府罷，移知候官縣，故相曾公亮鎮京兆，薦知涇陽縣，皆不赴。 丁外艱，家居講道。 數年，起為諸王宮教授。 求監鳳翔船務，制改宣義郎。
When Han Jiang served as commissioner to pacify Shaanxi and Hedong, he recruited Dajun as a scribe for confidential documents. When the commissioner's staff was dissolved, he was offered the magistracy of Houguan. Former chief minister Zeng Gongliang, then governing Jingzhao, recommended him for Jingyang. He declined both. After his mother's death he remained at home lecturing on the Way. Several years later he was recalled to serve as lecturer at the Princes' Palace. He petitioned to superintend the Fengxiang shipping office and was reclassified as Gentleman for Manifest Righteousness.
29
會伐西夏，鄜延轉運司檄為從事。 既出塞，轉運使李稷饋餉不繼，欲還安定取糧，使大鈞請於种諤。 諤曰：「吾受命將兵，安知糧道！ 萬一不繼，召稷來，與一劍耳。 」大鈞性剛直，即曰：「朝廷出師，去塞未遠，遂斬轉運使，無君父乎？ 」諤意折，強謂大鈞曰：「君欲以此報稷，先稷受禍矣！ 」大鈞怒曰：「公將以此言見恐邪？ 吾委身事主，死無所辭，正恐公過耳。 」諤見其直，乃好謂曰：「子乃爾邪？ 今聽汝矣！ 」始許稷還。 是時，微大鈞盛氣誚諤，稷且不免。 未幾，道得疾，卒，年五十二。
When a campaign was launched against Western Xia, the Fuyan transport office summoned him as a staff aide. After the army crossed the frontier, Transport Commissioner Li Ji could not keep supplies flowing. Wishing to return to Anding for grain, he sent Dajun to ask Zhong E. Zhong E said, "I was ordered to command troops. What do I know of supply lines!" If they fail, summon Li Ji here and I will give him a sword, that is all." Dajun, who was blunt by nature, replied at once, "The court has sent out this army. We are barely beyond the frontier and you would execute the transport commissioner? Have you no loyalty to ruler and father?" Zhong E was taken aback and blustered, "If you mean to settle a score for Li Ji this way, Li Ji will be the one harmed first!" Dajun flared up. "Do you think to frighten me with talk like that?" I have pledged myself to my superiors and would not shrink from death. What I fear is that you are going too far." Seeing his blunt honesty, Zhong E changed tone and said amiably, "So you are that sort of man?" "Very well—I grant your request!" Only then did he allow Li Ji to go back. Had Dajun not confronted Zhong E with such fierce indignation, Li Ji would scarcely have escaped with his life. Before long he fell ill on the road and died at the age of fifty-two.
30
大鈞從張載學，能守其師說而踐履之。 居父喪，衰麻葬祭，一本於禮。 後乃行於冠昏、膳飲、慶吊之間，節文粲然可觀，關中化之。 尤喜講明井田兵制，謂治道必自此始，悉撰次為圖籍，可見於用。 雖皆本於載，而能自信力行，載每歎其勇為不可及。
Dajun studied under Zhang Zai, held fast to his master's teachings, and lived by them. During mourning for his father, his dress, burial, and sacrifices all followed ritual to the letter. He later extended these observances to capping ceremonies, weddings, banquets, and occasions of congratulation and condolence. The forms were so clear and orderly that all of Guanzhong took them as a model. He was especially devoted to explaining the well-field system and military organization, arguing that good government must begin there. He compiled complete illustrated records that could be put to use. Though his ideas all stemmed from Zhang Zai, he had the confidence to act on them himself, and Zhang often sighed that his boldness was beyond comparison.
31
弟大臨
Younger brother: Lü Dalin
32
大臨，字與叔。 學於程頤，與謝良佐、游酢、楊時在程門，號「四先生」。 通《六經》，尤邃於《禮》。 每欲掇習三代遺文舊制，令可行，不為空言以拂世駭俗。 其論選舉曰：
Lü Dalin, whose courtesy name was Yushu, Studied under Cheng Yi. With Xie Liangzuo, You Zuo, and Yang Shi among Cheng's disciples he was known as one of the "Four Masters." He mastered the Six Classics and was especially profound in the Rites. He constantly sought to recover and practice the textual legacy and institutions of the Three Dynasties and make them workable—not empty talk that would shock society. On the subject of recruitment and appointment he wrote:
33
「古之長育人才者，以士眾多為樂； 今之主選舉者，以多為患。 古以禮聘士，常恐士之不至； 今以法待士，常恐士之競進。 古今豈有異哉。 蓋未之思爾。 夫為國之要，不過得人以治其事，如為治必欲得人，惟恐人才之不足，而何患於多？ 如治事皆任其責，惟恐士之不至，不憂其競進也。 今取人而用，不問其可任何事； 任人以事，不問其才之所堪。 故入流之路不勝其多，然為官擇士則常患乏才； 待次之吏歷歲不調，然考其職事則常患不治。 是所謂名實不稱，本末交戾。 如此而欲得人而事治，未之有也。 今欲立士規以養德厲行，更學制以量才進藝，定試法以區別能否，修辟法以興能備用，嚴舉法以核實得人，制考法以責任考功，庶幾可以漸復古矣。」
"In antiquity those who cultivated talent took joy in having many worthy men; Those who preside over recruitment today treat a large number as a problem. Antiquity recruited scholars through ritual courtesies and always feared they would not come; Today scholars are managed by regulations and one always fears they will scramble for advancement. How can antiquity and the present truly differ? It is only that people have not thought the matter through." The essence of governing a state is simply to obtain the right men to administer affairs. If one must have talent to govern well, one should fear only a shortage of men—why fret over having too many? When every post carries real responsibility, the only fear is that worthy men will not come—there is no reason to worry about their rushing forward. Today men are appointed without asking what tasks each can undertake; And tasks are assigned without asking what each man's talents can sustain. Thus the paths into office are more crowded than ever, yet when choosing men for posts there is a constant shortage of talent; While officials awaiting promotion go years without appointment, yet when their work is examined poor performance is the constant complaint. This is what is meant when name and reality fail to match and means and ends work against each other. To expect good government under such conditions has never been possible. We should set standards for scholars to cultivate virtue and discipline conduct, reform the school system to measure talent and advance learning, establish examinations to separate the capable from the incapable, refine recruitment to develop and deploy talent, tighten recommendation standards to ensure that appointments match merit, and create evaluation procedures to hold men accountable for results. In this way we might gradually return to the ways of antiquity."
34
富弼致政於家，為佛氏之學。 大臨與之書曰：「古者三公無職事，惟有德者居之，內則論道於朝，外則主教於鄉。 古之大人當是任者，必將以斯道覺斯民，成己以成物，豈以爵位進退、體力盛衰為之變哉？ 今大道未明，人趨異學，不入於莊，則入於釋。 疑聖人為未盡善，輕禮義為不足學，人倫不明，萬物憔悴，此老成大人惻隱存心之時。 以道自任，振起壞俗，在公之力，宜無難矣。 若夫移精變氣，務求長年，此山谷避世之士獨善其身者之所好，豈世之所以望於公者哉？ 」弼謝之。
After retiring from office, Fu Bi devoted himself at home to Buddhist studies. Dalin wrote to him: "In antiquity the Three Excellencies had no routine administrative duties; only men of virtue filled them. Within the court they expounded the Way; abroad they led instruction in their districts. The great men who accepted such responsibility sought to awaken the people through the Way, perfecting themselves to perfect the world. How could the rise and fall of office, or the vigor or decline of one's body, change that calling? Today the Way is not yet fully understood and people flock to heterodox teachings—if not to Zhuangzi, then to Buddhism. They doubt the sages were less than perfect and dismiss rites and righteousness as unworthy of study. Human relations are obscured and the world languishes. This is the moment when a seasoned elder should act from humane concern. To take the Way upon yourself and revive a fallen age is well within your power—it should not be difficult at all. As for refining the spirit and altering the breath in pursuit of long life—that is the pursuit of recluses who withdraw to the hills and care only for themselves. Is that truly what the world expects of you?" Fu Bi thanked him for the admonition.
35
元祐中，為太學博士，遷秘書省正字。 范祖禹薦其好學修身如古人，可備勸學，未及用而卒。
During the Yuanyou era he served as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and was promoted to Correcting Clerk of the Secretariat. Fan Zuyu recommended him for his ancient-style devotion to learning and self-cultivation, saying he could serve in promoting scholarship, but before he could be appointed Dalin died.
36
劉摯，字莘老，永靜東光人。 兒時，父居正課以書，朝夕不少間。 或謂：「君止一子，獨不可少寬邪？ 」居正曰：「正以一子，不可縱也。 」十歲而孤，鞠於外氏，就學東平，因家焉。
Liu Zhi, whose courtesy name was Xinlao, was a native of Dongguang in Yongjing Circuit. As a boy his father Juzheng drilled him in his studies without respite from morning till night. Someone said, "You have only this one son. Surely you could be a little easier on him?" Juzheng replied, "Precisely because I have only one son I must not indulge him." He was orphaned at ten, raised by his mother's family, and went to study at Dongping, where he settled.
37
嘉祐中，擢甲科，歷冀州南宮令。 縣比不得入，俗化凋敝，其賦甚重，輸絹匹折稅錢五百，綿兩折錢三十，民多破產。 摯援例旁郡，條請裁以中價。 轉運使怒，將劾之。 摯固請曰：「獨一州六邑被此苦，決非法意，但朝廷不知耳。 」遂告於朝。 三司使包拯奏從其議，自是絹為錢千三百，綿七十有六。 民歡呼至泣下，曰：「劉長官活我！ 」是時，摯與信都令李沖、清河令黃莘皆以治行聞，人稱為「河朔三令」。
In the Jiayou era he passed the examinations in the top class and served as magistrate of Nangong in Jizhou. The county ranked below the standard for tax assessment; customs were decayed and levies crushing—a bolt of silk was assessed at five hundred cash and two ounces of cotton at thirty, and many families were ruined. Citing precedents from neighboring prefectures, Zhi petitioned to set conversion rates at fair market prices. The transport commissioner was furious and prepared to impeach him. Zhi pressed his case: "Only one prefecture and six counties suffer this hardship. That cannot be the intent of the law—the court simply does not know." He then brought the matter before the court. Privy Treasurer Bao Zheng memorialized in favor of his proposal. From then on silk was assessed at thirteen hundred cash and cotton at seventy-six. The people shouted for joy until they wept, crying, "Magistrate Liu has saved our lives!" At that time Zhi, together with Li Chong of Xindu and Huang Shen of Qinghe, were all known for excellent administration and were called the "Three Magistrates of Heshuo."
38
徙江陵觀察推官，用韓琦薦，得館閣校勘。 王安石一見器異之，擢檢正中書禮房，默默非所好也。 才月餘，為監察御史裏行，欣然就職，歸語家人曰：「趣裝，毋為安居計。 」未及陛對，即奏論：「亳州獄起不止，小人意在傾富弼以市進，今弼已得罪，願少寬之。 」又言：「程昉開漳河，調發猝迫，人不堪命。 趙子幾擅升畿縣等，使納役錢，縣民日數千人遮訴宰相，京師喧然，何以示四方？ 張靚、王廷老擅增兩浙役錢，督賦嚴急，人情嗟怨。 此皆欲以羡餘希賞，願行顯責，明朝廷本無聚斂之意。」
He was transferred to investigating clerk at Jiangling and, on Han Qi's recommendation, received appointment as collator in the Palace Library. Wang Anshi was impressed at first meeting and promoted him to reviser in the Secretariat-Chancellery's Rites Section, but Zhi quietly found the post uncongenial. After little more than a month he was appointed provisional investigating censor. He took the post gladly and told his family on returning home, "Pack up—we must not plan on settling in." Before his first audience he memorialized: "The case at Bozhou keeps resurfacing. Petty men mean to ruin Fu Bi for their own advancement. Now that Bi has already been punished, I beg you to show some leniency." He also said, "Cheng Fang's opening of the Zhang River canal was rushed through with sudden conscription; the people could not bear it." Zhao Ziji arbitrarily raised the grade of metropolitan counties and demanded corvée payments. Thousands of county residents daily blocked the roads to appeal to the chief councillor, stirring uproar in the capital. What message does this send to the realm? Zhang Liang and Wang Tinglao unilaterally raised corvée payments in the Two Zhes, enforcing collection with harsh urgency and stirring widespread resentment. All of these men seek rewards through surplus revenue. I urge clear and public punishment to show that the court never intended to enrich itself through exactions."
39
及入見，神宗面賜褒諭。 因問：「卿從學王安石邪？ 安石極稱卿器識。 」對曰：「臣東北人，少孤獨學，不識安石也。 」退而上疏曰：
At his audience Shenzong personally praised and commended him. The emperor asked, "Did you study under Wang Anshi?" Anshi speaks very highly of your talent and judgment." He replied, "I am from the northeast. Orphaned as a youth, I studied on my own. I do not know Wang Anshi." On withdrawing he submitted another memorial:
40
「君子小人之分，在義利而已。 小人才非不足用，特心之所向，不在乎義。 故希賞之志，每在事先； 奉公之心，每在私後。 陛下有勸農之意，今變而為煩擾； 陛下有均役之意，今倚以為聚斂。 其有愛君之心，憂國之言者，皆無以容於其間。 今天下有喜於敢為，有樂於無事。 彼以此為流俗，此以彼為亂常。 畏義者以進取為可恥，嗜利者以守道為無能。 此風浸成，漢、唐黨禍必起矣。 惟君子為能通天下之志。 臣願陛下虛心平聽，審察好惡，前日意以為是者，今更察其非； 前日意以為短者，今更用其長。 稍抑虛譁輕偽、志近忘遠、幸於苟合之人，漸察忠厚慎重、難進易退、可與有為之士。 收過與不及之俗，使會於大中之道，則施設變化，惟陛下號令之而已。」
"The line between gentleman and petty man is drawn between righteousness and profit, nothing more." Petty men are often capable enough; what they lack is any orientation toward righteousness. Their eagerness for reward always comes before the public good; Their devotion to public duty always comes after private interest. Your Majesty meant to encourage agriculture, yet it has become vexation and turmoil; Your Majesty meant to equalize corvée duties, yet they have become a tool for revenue extraction. Those who truly love the ruler and speak for the state's welfare find no place among them. Today the realm divides between those who delight in daring action and those who delight in doing nothing. Each side calls the other vulgar or disruptive of proper order. Men who revere righteousness are mocked for seeking office; men who crave profit dismiss integrity as weakness. If this spirit takes hold, the factional disasters of Han and Tang will surely come again. Only the gentleman can truly unite the minds of the realm. I beg Your Majesty to listen with an open mind and weigh preferences carefully—what seemed right yesterday, examine today for its errors; What seemed a failing yesterday, employ today for its strengths. Restrain somewhat the brash, superficial, short-sighted men who grasp at easy compromise, and gradually discern the loyal, prudent men who are slow to advance and quick to withdraw—men capable of real achievement. Reconcile excess and deficiency in custom and bring them together in the great middle Way. Then whatever reforms you undertake will depend on Your Majesty's command alone."
41
又論率錢助役、官自雇人有十害，其略曰：
He also set out ten evils of the corvée-assistance levy and official hiring of laborers, in summary as follows:
42
「天下州縣戶役，虛實重輕不同。 今等以為率，則非一法所能齊； 隨其所宜，各自立法，則紛擾散殊，何以統率？ 一也。 新法謂版籍不實，故令別立等第。 且舊籍既不可信，今何以得其無失？ 不獨搔擾生事患，將使富輸少，貧輸多，二也。 天下上戶少，中戶多。 上戶役數而重，故以助錢為幸。 中戶役簡而輕，下戶役所不及。 今概使輸錢，則為不幸，三也。 有司欲多得雇錢，而患上戶之寡，故不用舊籍，臨時升降，使民何以堪命？ 四也。 歲有豐凶，而役人有定數，助錢不可闕。 非若稅賦有倚閣、減放之期，五也。 穀、麥、布、帛，歲有所出，而助法必輸見錢，六也。 二稅科買，色目已多，又概率錢以竭其所有，斯民無有悅而願為農者，戶口當日耗失，七也。 僥倖者又將緣法生奸，如近日兩浙倍科錢數，自以為功，八也。 差法近者十餘年，遠或二十年，乃一充役，民安習之久矣。 今官自雇人，直重則民不堪，輕則人不願，不免以力毆之就役，九也。 且役人必用鄉戶，家有常產，則必知自愛； 性既愚實，則罕有盜欺。 今一切雇募，但得輕猾浮偽之人，巧詐相資，何所不至？ 十也。」
"Household corvée obligations differ from place to place in burden and exemption." If a single uniform rate is imposed, no one law can make them equal; If each locality legislates as it sees fit, confusion and inconsistency multiply—how can the system be governed as one? That is the first evil. The new law holds that household registers are unreliable and therefore orders new gradings. If the old registers were untrustworthy, why should the new ones be free of error? This will not only stir up trouble but also make the rich pay less and the poor pay more. That is the second evil. Upper households are few throughout the realm; middle households are many. Upper households bear numerous and heavy corvée duties, so they welcome paying money in lieu. Middle households face lighter duties; lower households are barely touched. To require all alike to pay money is a misfortune for them. That is the third evil. Officials want more hiring money but worry that upper households are too few, so they disregard old registers and manipulate grades on the spot. How can the people bear it? That is the fourth evil. Harvests may be rich or poor, yet corvée quotas stay fixed and the money in lieu of service cannot be waived. Unlike tax levies, which may be deferred or reduced, no such relief exists here. That is the fifth evil. Grain, wheat, cloth, and silk are produced every year, yet the assistance law demands cash on the barrelhead. That is the sixth evil. The two taxes and state purchases already cover many categories, and now proportional cash levies drain whatever people still hold. None among the common folk will gladly remain farmers, and household registers will shrink day by day. That is the seventh evil. Opportunists will exploit the law to commit fraud, as when officials in Liangzhe recently doubled cash levies and counted it as achievement. That is the eighth evil. Under the old dispatch system, a man might serve corvée only once in ten-odd years nearby, or once in twenty farther out, and the people had long grown used to it. Now the government hires labor itself. If wages are set high the people cannot afford them; if set low, no one will come—and officials cannot avoid driving men into service by force. That is the ninth evil. Moreover, corvée workers ought to be drawn from native households; families with fixed property know how to value themselves. Simple and honest by nature, they rarely steal or cheat. Now with universal hiring, one gets only frivolous, cunning, and pretentious men who abet one another in deceit—what would they stop at? That is the tenth evil."
43
會御史中丞楊繪亦言其非，安石使張琥作十難以詰之，琥辭不為，司農曾布請為之。 既作十難，且劾摯、繪欺誕懷向背。 詔問狀，繪懼謝罪。 摯奮曰：「為人臣豈可壓於權勢，使天子不知利害之實！ 」即條對所難，以伸其說。 且曰：「臣待罪言責，採士民之說以聞於上，職也。 今有司遽令分析，是使之較是非，爭勝負，交口相直，無乃辱陛下耳目之任哉！ 所謂向背，則臣所向者義，所背者利； 所向者君父，所背者權臣。 願以臣章並司農奏宣示百官，考定當否。 如臣言有取，幸早施行，若稍涉欺罔，甘就竄逐。 」不報。 摯明日覆上疏曰：
About then Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Hui also spoke against the policy. Anshi had Zhang Hu draft ten objections to cross-examine them, but Hu declined, and Minister of Revenue Zeng Bu offered to do it instead. After drafting the ten objections, he also impeached Zhi and Hui for deception and divided loyalties. An edict demanded their written response, and Hui, frightened, apologized. Zhi responded forcefully: "As a subject, how can one be cowed by power and leave the Son of Heaven ignorant of what is truly harmful or beneficial! " He then answered each objection point by point to make his case. He also said: "Your servant holds office charged with remonstrance; to gather what gentry and commoners say and report it upward is my duty. Now the authorities hastily order us to debate in detail, forcing us to contest right and wrong and refute one another—is this not an insult to Your Majesty's role as eyes and ears! As for what is called divided loyalty, what I turn toward is righteousness and what I turn against is profit; What I turn toward is my sovereign and father; what I turn against is the minister who holds power. I ask that my memorial and the Minister of Revenue's submission be shown to all officials so they may judge what is right. If anything in my words proves sound, I pray it be put into effect at once; if it involves the slightest deception, I willingly accept exile. " No reply came. The next day Zhi submitted another memorial, saying:
44
「陛下起居言動，躬蹈德禮，夙夜厲精，以親庶政。 天下未至於安且治者，誰致之耶？ 陛下注意以望太平，而自以太平為己任，得君專政者是也。 二三年間，開闔動搖，舉天下無一物得安其所者。 蓋自青苗之議起，而天下始有聚斂之疑； 青苗之議未允，而均輸之法行； 均輸之法方擾，而邊鄙之謀動； 邊鄙之禍未艾，而助役之事興。 至於求水利，行淤田，并州縣，興事起新，難以遍舉。 其議財，則市井屠販之人，皆召至政事堂。 其征利，則下至歷日，而官自鬻之。 推此而往，不可究言。 輕用名器，淆混賢否：忠厚老成者，擯之為無能； 狹少儇辯者，取之為可用； 守道憂國者，謂之流俗； 敗常害民者，謂之通變。 凡政府謀議經畫，除用進退，獨與一掾屬決之，然後落筆。 同列預聞，反在其後。 故奔走乞丐之人，其門如市。 今西夏之款未入，反側之兵未安，三邊瘡痍，流潰未定。 河北大旱，諸路大水，民勞財乏，縣官減耗。 聖上憂勤念治之時，而政事如此，皆大臣誤陛下，而大臣所用者，誤大臣也。」
"Your Majesty's daily conduct and speech embody virtue and ritual; morning and night you exert yourself to attend personally to the affairs of government. That the realm has not yet reached security and good order—who has brought this about? Your Majesty fixes his attention on peace, yet those who hold the emperor's trust and monopolize government take peace as their own charge. In two or three years everything has been thrown open and shut again; nothing under heaven has found a settled place. It began with debate over the Green Sprouts loans, and the realm first grew suspicious of exaction; Before the Green Sprouts debate was settled, the equal-transport law was put into effect; While the equal-transport law still stirred turmoil, frontier schemes were set in motion; Before frontier calamities had ceased, the labor-assistance policy was launched. As for seeking waterworks, practicing silt-field reclamation, merging prefectures and counties, and launching one new venture after another—these cannot all be enumerated. When finances were deliberated, butchers and peddlers from the market streets were all summoned to the Hall of Affairs. When profit was pursued, it extended even to almanacs, which the government itself sold. Push this further and it defies full recounting. Titles of office are lightly bestowed, blurring the worthy and unworthy: men of loyalty, honesty, and seasoned judgment are pushed aside as incompetent; Narrow-minded young glib debaters are taken as useful; Those who hold to the Way and worry for the state are called vulgar conformists; Those who ruin norms and harm the people are called men of practical flexibility. All government planning, appointments, promotions, and dismissals are decided alone with one clerk-assistant, and only then put to paper. Colleagues hear of them only afterward. Hence those who bustle and beg flock to his gate like a market. Now the Western Xia have not yet submitted in good faith; mutinous troops are not yet pacified; the three frontiers are wounded and bleeding, and the turmoil has not yet been stanched. Hebei suffers great drought; many circuits face floods; the people are exhausted and funds depleted; government stores dwindle. At a time when the Sage Sovereign is diligent in his concern for governance, yet affairs stand thus—all this is the great ministers misleading Your Majesty, and what the great ministers employ misleads the great ministers."
45
疏奏，安石欲竄之嶺外，神宗不聽，但謫監衡州鹽倉。 繪出知鄭州，琥亦落職。 摯乞詣鄆遷葬，然後奔赴貶所，許之。
When the memorial was submitted, Anshi wished to banish him beyond the Lingnan, but Emperor Shenzong did not assent and demoted him instead to supervise the Hengzhou salt depot. Hui was sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou, and Hu was also dismissed from office. Zhi requested permission to go to Yun to relocate a burial and then proceed to his place of exile, and this was granted.
46
先是，倉吏與綱兵奸利相市，鹽中雜以偽惡，遠人未嘗食善鹽。 摯悉意核視，且儲其羡以為賞，弊減什七。 父老目為「學士鹽」。 久之，簽書南京判官。 會司農新令，盡斥賣天下祠廟，依坊場河渡法收淨利。 南京閼伯廟歲錢四十六貫，微子廟十三貫。 摯歎曰：「一至於此！ 」往見留守張方平曰：「獨不能為朝廷言之耶？ 」方平瞿然，託摯為奏曰：「閼伯遷商丘，主祀大火，火為國家盛德所乘，歷世尊為大祀。 微子，宋始封之君，開國此地，本朝受命，建號所因。 又有雙廟者，唐張巡、許遠孤城死賊，能捍大患。 今若令承買小人規利，冗褻瀆慢，何所不為，歲收微細，實損大體。 慾望留此三廟，以慰邦人崇奉之意。 」從之。 又見《方平傳》。
Earlier, depot clerks and transport soldiers traded corrupt profits; salt was adulterated with spurious and inferior matter, and people from afar had never tasted good salt. Zhi inspected it thoroughly, set aside surpluses as rewards, and reduced malfeasance by seven-tenths. The elders called it "Scholar's Salt." After some time, he was appointed Acting Secretary and Judge of Nanjing. It happened that a new order from the Ministry of Revenue required the sale of all shrine temples nationwide, collecting net profits by the method used for licensed shops and ferry crossings. In Nanjing, the Quebo Shrine brought in forty-six strings per year and the Weizi Shrine thirteen strings. Zhi sighed and said: "Things have come to this! " He went to see the garrison commander Zhang Fangping and said: "Can you not speak to the court about this? " Fangping started, and entrusted Zhi to memorialize: "Quebo moved to Shangqiu and presides over the Sacrifice to the Great Fire; fire is borne upon by the state's abundant virtue and has always been honored as a great sacrifice. Weizi was the first enfeoffed lord of Song; he founded the state on this ground; our dynasty received the Mandate and took its founding designation from here. There is also the Twin Shrine: Tang's Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan died defending a lone city against the rebels and were able to ward off great calamity. If petty profiteers are now allowed to lease these for gain, they will profane and insult without limit; the annual revenue is trifling, yet the harm to the larger principle is real. I wish to retain these three shrines to satisfy the people's wish to honor them. " This was approved. This is also recorded in the Biography of Fangping.
47
入同知太常禮院。 元豐初，改集賢校理、知大宗正寺丞，為開封府推官。 神宗開天章閣，議新官制，除至禮部郎中，曰：「此南宮舍人，非他曹比，無出劉摯者。 」即命之。 俄遷右司郎中。
He entered service as Associate Administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. At the beginning of the Yuanfeng era, he was made Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, and served as investigating officer of the Kaifeng Prefecture office. Emperor Shenzong opened the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and deliberated on a new bureaucratic system; when the appointment reached Director of the Ministry of Rites, he said: "This is a Southern Palace Academy drafter—not comparable to other offices; none surpasses Liu Zhi. " He was immediately appointed. Soon he was promoted to Director of the Right Office.
48
他日講筵進讀，至仁宗不避庚戌臨奠張士遜，侍讀曰：「國朝故事，多避國音。 國朝角音，木也，故畏庚辛。 」哲宗問：「果當避否？ 」摯進曰：「陰陽拘忌，聖人不取，如正月祈穀必用上辛，此豈可改也？ 漢章帝以反支日受章奏，唐太宗以辰日哭張公謹，仁宗不避庚戌日，皆陛下所宜取法。 」哲宗然之。
Another day, during lectured readings at court, they came to Emperor Renzong's not avoiding the gengxu day when attending Zhang Shisun's funeral; the Reader said: "Our dynasty's custom often avoids the nation's homophonic taboos. The nation's pitch is jue, which belongs to wood; hence we fear geng and xin. " Emperor Zhezong asked: "Should it truly be avoided? " Zhi advanced and said: "The sages do not heed yin-yang superstitions; in the first month the grain prayer must use the upper xin day—could that be altered? Emperor Zhang of Han received memorials on fanzhi days; Emperor Taizong of Tang wept for Zhang Gongjin on a chen day; Renzong did not avoid the gengxu day—all models Your Majesty should follow. " The emperor agreed.
49
摯又言：「諫官御史員缺未補，監察雖滿六員，專以察治官司公事，而不預言責。 臣請增補臺諫，並許言事。 」時蔡確、章惇在政地，與司馬光不相能。 摯因久旱上言：「《洪範》：『庶徵肅，時雨若。 』《五行傳》：『政緩則冬旱。 』今廟堂大臣，情志乖暌，議政之際，依違排狠，語播於外，可謂不肅。 政令二三，舒緩不振。 比日日青無光，風霾昏曀，上天警告，皆非小變。 願進忠良、通壅塞，以答天戒。」
Zhi also said: "Censor and remonstrance posts remain unfilled; though the six investigating censors are complete, they are devoted only to inspecting official business and do not share remonstrance duties. I ask to fill the bureau and remonstrance posts and allow them all to speak on affairs. " At that time Cai Que and Zhang Dun held power and were at odds with Sima Guang. Because of prolonged drought, Zhi submitted: "The Hong Fan states: 'When the various signs are orderly, timely rain follows.' 'The Treatise on the Five Phases states: 'When government is lax, winter drought follows.' Today the ministers in the hall are at odds in mind and feeling; in deliberating policy they waver and clash harshly, and their words spread abroad—this can be called disorderly. Edicts come in twos and threes, slack and without vigor. Lately the sun has shown no color; wind and haze have dimmed the sky—the warnings of heaven are no small change. I pray you advance the loyal and good, clear blockages, and answer heaven's admonition."
50
蔡確為山陵使，神宗靈駕發引前夕不入宿，摯劾之，不報。 及使回，既朝即視事，摯又奏確不引咎自劾。 無何，確上表自陳，嘗請收拔當世之耆艾，以陪輔王室，蠲省有司之煩碎，以慰安民心。 摯謂：「使確誠有是請，不言於先朝，為不忠之罪； 言於今日，為取容之計。 誠無是請，則欺君莫大於此。 」又疏確過惡大略有十，論章惇凶悍輕侻，無大臣體，皆罷去。
Cai Que served as commissioner for the imperial mausoleum; on the eve before the late Shenzong's coffin procession departed, he did not stay overnight on duty. Zhi impeached him, but no response came. When the commission returned, Que went straight from court audience to conduct business. Zhi again memorialized that Que had not accepted blame and impeached himself. Before long, Que submitted a self-account, claiming he had once asked to gather worthy elders of the age to assist the royal house and reduce the petty burdens of officials to comfort the people's hearts. Zhi said: "If Que truly made such a request and did not speak of it under the previous reign, that is the crime of disloyalty; To speak of it today is a calculation to curry favor. If he truly made no such request, then no deception of the sovereign is greater than this. " He also listed roughly ten major faults of Que and argued that Zhang Dun was fierce, reckless, and flippant, lacking the bearing of a great minister—both should be dismissed.
51
初，神宗更新學制，養士以千數，有司立為約束，過於煩密。 摯上疏曰：
Initially, Shenzong reformed the school system and supported scholars by the thousands; the authorities established regulations that were excessively detailed and burdensome. Zhi submitted a memorial, saying:
52
「學校為育材首善之地，教化所從出，非行法之所。 雖群居眾聚，帥而齊之，不可無法，亦有禮義存焉。 先帝體道制法，超漢軼唐，養士之盛，比隆三代。 然而比以太學屢起獄訟，有司緣此造為法禁，煩苛愈於治獄，條目多於防盜，上下疑貳，以求苟免。 甚可怪者，博士、諸生禁不相見，教諭無所施，質問無所從，月巡所隸之齋而已。 齋舍既不一，隨經分隸，則又《易》博士兼巡《禮》齋，《詩》博士兼巡《書》齋，所至備禮請問，相與揖諾，亦或不交一言而退，以防私請，以杜賄賂。 學校如此，豈先帝所以造士之意哉？ 治天下者，遇人以君子、長者之道，則下必有君子、長者之行而應乎上。 若以小人、犬彘遇之，彼將以小人、犬彘自為，而況以此行於學校之間乎？ 願罷其制。」
"Schools are the foremost ground for nurturing talent, the source from which instruction flows—not a place for enforcing penal law. Though many live together in groups and must be led to order and cannot be without rules, rites and propriety also dwell there. The late emperor embodied the Way and framed laws, surpassing Han and exceeding Tang; the flourishing of scholars rivaled the Three Dynasties. Yet recently, because lawsuits have repeatedly arisen at the National University, officials have used this to fabricate prohibitions—more burdensome than governing prisons, more numerous in articles than guarding against theft. Above and below are suspicious and doubtful, seeking only to escape blame. Most strange of all: doctors of learning and students are forbidden to meet; instruction cannot be applied; there is no channel for asking questions—they merely make monthly rounds of the dormitories under their charge. Since dormitories differ and assignments follow the classics, a Doctor of Changes also inspects the Ritual dormitory and a Doctor of Odes also inspects the Documents dormitory. Where they arrive they observe full ceremony and make inquiries, exchange bows and assents, yet sometimes exchange not a single word before departing—to guard against private requests and shut out bribery. When schools are thus, is this the late emperor's intent in nurturing scholars? Those who govern the realm, if they treat others with the courtesy due to gentlemen and elders, will surely find those below responding with the conduct of gentlemen and elders in turn. If you treat them as petty men or dogs and swine, they will behave as petty men and dogs—and how much worse when such treatment is practiced in the schools? I ask that this system be abolished."
53
又請雜用經義、詩賦取士，復賢良方正科，罷常平、免役，引朱光庭、王岩叟為言官。 執憲數月，正色彈劾，多所貶黜，百僚敬憚，時人以比包拯、呂晦。
He also petitioned to select officials through a mixture of Classic exegesis, poetry, and rhapsody; to restore the Exemplary and Upright Worthies examination; to abolish the Ever-Normal Granary and corvée-exemption schemes; and to bring in Zhu Guangting and Wang Yansou as remonstrating officials. In the censorate for several months he impeached with stern countenance and demoted many officials; the whole bureaucracy respected and feared him, and contemporaries compared him to Bao Zheng and Lü Hui.
54
元祐元年，擢御史中丞。 摯上疏曰：「上之所好，下必有甚。 朝廷意在總覈，下必有刻薄之行； 朝廷務在寬大，下必有苟簡之事。 習俗懷利，迎意趨和，所為近似，而非上之意本然也。 今因革之政本殊，而觀望之俗故在。 昨差役初行，監司已有迎合爭先，不校利害，一概定差，一路為之騷動者。 朝廷察其如此，固已黜之矣。 以是觀之，大約類此。 向來黜責數人者，皆以非法掊克，市進害民，然非欲使之漫不省事。 昧者不達，矯枉過正，顧可不為之禁哉？ 請立監司考績之制。」
In the first year of Yuanyou he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief. Zhi submitted a memorial, saying, "Whatever those above favor, those below will surely surpass. When the court intends comprehensive audits, those below will surely behave harshly; When the court stresses clemency, those below will surely grow slack and perfunctory. People bent on gain read the mood and rush to conform; their actions merely resemble the aim of policy and do not reflect what those above truly intend. The policies of repeal and reform are now fundamentally different, yet the old habit of watching and waiting endures. When the corvée system was first introduced, circuit commissioners were already vying to ingratiate themselves, heedless of benefit or harm, fixing assignments wholesale and throwing entire circuits into turmoil. Seeing this, the court had already dismissed them from office. Judging by this example, the pattern is much the same elsewhere. Those recently dismissed had all extorted unlawfully, buying advancement at the people's expense—but the purpose was not to leave them indifferent and neglectful of their duties. The dull-witted fail to understand and overcorrect past abuses—is this not something that must be stopped? I ask that a system for evaluating circuit commissioners be established."
55
拜尚書右丞，連進左丞、中書侍郎，遷門下侍郎。 胡宗愈除右丞，諫議大夫王覿疏其非是，宣仁后怒，將加深譴。 摯開救甚力，簾中厲聲曰：「若有人以門下侍郎為奸邪，甘受之否？ 」摯曰：「陛下審察毀譽每如此，天下幸甚！ 然願顧大體，宗愈進用，自有公議，必致貶諫官而後進，恐宗愈亦所未安。 」宣仁后意解，覿得補郡守。
He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, then successively Left Vice Director and Vice Minister of the Secretariat, and was transferred to Vice Minister of the Chancellery. When Hu Zongyu was appointed Right Vice Director, Remonstrance Grandee Wang Di memorialized against the appointment; Empress Dowager Xuanren grew angry and was ready to punish him severely. Zhi interceded for him vigorously. From behind the curtain came a stern voice: "If someone accuses the Vice Minister of the Chancellery of treachery, would you willingly accept that? Zhi replied, "When Your Majesty scrutinizes slander and praise this closely, the realm is greatly fortunate! Yet I hope Your Majesty will consider the larger situation. Zongyu's advancement would naturally provoke public debate; to demote the remonstrating official before promoting him would leave even Zongyu ill at ease. Empress Dowager Xuanren's anger eased, and Wang Di was appointed to a prefectural post.
56
摯與同列奏事論人才，摯曰：「人才難得，能否不一。 性忠實而才識有餘，上也； 才識不逮而忠實有餘，次也； 有才而難保，可藉以集事，又其次也。 懷邪觀望，隨時勢改變，此小人也，終不可用。 」哲宗及宣仁后曰：「卿常能如此用人，國家何憂！ 」六年，拜尚書右僕射。
While presenting business with his colleagues, Zhi spoke on the question of talent: "Good men are hard to find; capacities vary. Men loyal at heart with ample talent and judgment—the best; Men whose talent falls short but whose loyalty is ample—the next; Men of talent who cannot be fully trusted, yet can still be used to get things done—the grade below that. Men who harbor wickedness, watch the wind, and shift with the times—these are petty men and should never be employed. Emperor Zhezong and Empress Dowager Xuanren said, "If you always appoint men this wisely, what need has the state to worry! In the sixth year he was appointed Right Director of the Department of State Affairs.
57
摯性峭直，有氣節，通達明銳，觸機輒發，不為利怵威誘。 自初輔政至為相，修嚴憲法，辨白邪正，專以人物處心，孤立一意，不受謁請。 子弟親戚入官，皆令赴銓部以格調選，未嘗以干朝廷。 與呂大防同位，國家大事，多決於大防，惟進退士大夫，實執其柄。 然持心少恕，勇於去惡，竟為朋讒奇中。 先是，邢恕謫官永州，以書抵摯。 摯故與恕善，答其書，有「永州佳處，第往以俟休復」之語。 排岸官茹東濟，傾險人也，有求於摯，不得，見其書，陰錄以示御史中丞鄭雍、侍御史楊畏。 二人方交章擊摯，遂箋釋其語上之，曰：「『休復』者，語出《周易》，『以俟休復』者，俟他日太皇太后復子明辟也。 」又章惇諸子故與摯之子游，摯亦間與之接。 雍、畏謂延見接納，為牢籠之計，以冀後福。 宣仁后於是面喻摯曰：「言者謂卿交通匪人，為異日地，卿當一心王室。 若章惇者，雖以宰相處之，未必樂也。 」摯皇懼退，上章自辨，執政亦為之言。 宣仁后曰：「垂簾之初，摯排斥奸邪，實為忠直。 但此二事，非所當為也。 」以觀文殿學士罷知鄆州。 給事中朱光庭駁云：「摯忠義自奮，朝廷擢之大位，一旦以疑而罷，天下不見其過。 」光庭亦罷。 七年，徙大名，又為雍等所遏，徙知青州。
Zhi was stern and upright by nature, a man of integrity—perceptive, sharp, and quick to act when provoked, unmoved by profit or intimidation. From his first entry into government through his years as chief minister, he rigorously enforced the law, distinguished wicked from upright, judged men and affairs on their merits alone, stood apart in purpose, and accepted no private solicitations. When sons, brothers, and kinsmen sought office, he made them go through the Board of Appointments and compete under the regular rules, never using his influence at court. Though he shared power with Lü Dafang, most major affairs were decided by Dafang; only in advancing and dismissing scholar-officials did Zhi truly hold the reins. Yet he was sparing in mercy, bold in removing evil, and in the end was felled by a strange stroke of factional slander. Earlier, Xing Shu had been demoted to Yongzhou and wrote to Zhi. Zhi had long been friendly with Shu and replied with words to the effect: "Yongzhou has its charms—simply go there and wait until restoration after rest." Ru Dongji, a bank commissioner of treacherous character, had sought favors from Zhi and been refused; seeing the letter, he secretly copied it and showed it to Vice Censor-in-Chief Zheng Yong and Attending Censor Yang Wei. The two were already submitting memorial upon memorial attacking Zhi. They annotated his words and reported to the throne: "'Restoration after rest' is a phrase from the Book of Changes; 'waiting for restoration after rest' means waiting for the Empress Dowager one day to restore the Emperor to enlightened rule. Zhang Dun's sons had also studied with Zhi's son, and Zhi occasionally received them as well. Yong and Wei claimed these audiences and associations were a scheme to cultivate allies in hope of future advantage. Empress Dowager Xuanren then spoke to Zhi directly: "Critics say you consort with disreputable men and are laying groundwork for the future. You must give your whole heart to the throne. Someone like Zhang Dun—even if placed in the position of chief minister—would not necessarily be content. Zhi withdrew in great alarm and submitted a memorial in self-defense; the chief ministers also spoke on his behalf. Empress Dowager Xuanren said, "At the start of the regency, Zhi drove out wicked men and was truly loyal and upright. But in these two matters he did what ought not to have been done. He was stripped of his post as Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literary Works and sent out as prefect of Yanzhou. Supervising Secretariat Drafter Zhu Guangting objected: "Zhi rose through his own loyalty; the court elevated him to the highest rank, yet now dismisses him on mere suspicion—the realm sees no fault in him. Guangting was dismissed as well. In the seventh year he was transferred to Daming; obstructed again by Zheng Yong and others, he was moved to serve as prefect of Qingzhou.
58
紹聖初，來之邵、周秩論摯變法、棄地罪，奪職知黃州，再貶光祿卿，分司南京，蘄州居住。 將行，語諸子曰：「上用章惇，吾且得罪。 若惇顧國事，不遷怒百姓，但責吾曹，死無所恨。 正慮意在報復，法令益峻，奈天下何！ 」憂形於色，無一言及遷謫意。 四年，陷邢恕之謗，貶鼎州團練副使，新州安置。 惟一子從。 家人涕泣願侍，皆不聽。 至數月，以疾卒，年六十八。
At the start of the Shaosheng era, Lai Zhishao and Zhou Zhi indicted Zhi for altering the reforms and abandoning territory; he was stripped of office and made prefect of Huangzhou, then demoted again to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with detached service at the Southern Capital and ordered to reside at Qizhou. Before departing he told his sons, "The Emperor is employing Zhang Dun—I am sure to be punished. If Dun keeps the nation's interests in mind, does not vent his anger on the people, and holds only us accountable, I shall die without regret. What I truly fear is that he intends revenge, that laws grow ever harsher—what will become of the realm! Worry showed plainly on his face; he spoke not a word about his own exile. In the fourth year he was caught up in Xing Shu's calumny, demoted to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Dingzhou, and ordered to settle at Xinzhou. Only one son went with him. His family wept and begged to accompany him, but he refused them all. After several months he died of illness, at the age of sixty-eight.
59
初，摯與呂大防為相，文及甫居喪，在洛怨望，服除，恐不得京官，抵書邢恕曰：「改月遂除，入朝之計未可必。 當塗猜怨於鷹揚者益深，其徒實繁。 司馬昭之心，路人所知也，濟之以『粉昆』，必欲以眇躬為甘心快意之地，可為寒心。 」其謂司馬昭者，指呂大防獨當國久； 『粉昆』者，世以駙馬都尉為『粉侯』，韓嘉彥尚主，以兄忠彥為『粉昆』也。 恕以書示蔡碩、蔡渭，渭上書訟摯及大防等十餘人陷其父確，謀危宗社，引及甫書為證。 時章惇、蔡卞誣造元祐諸人事不已，因是欲殺摯及梁燾、王岩叟等。 以為摯有廢立之意，遂起同文館獄，用蔡京、安惇雜治，逮問及甫。 及甫元祐末德大防除權侍郎，又忠彥雖罷，哲宗眷之未衰，乃託其亡父嘗說司馬昭指劉摯，「粉」謂王岩叟面白如粉，「昆」謂梁燾字況之，「況」猶「兄」也。 又問實狀，但云：「疑其事勢如此。 」會摯卒，京奏不及考驗，遂免其子官，與家屬徙英州，凡三年，死於瘴者十人。
Earlier, while Zhi and Lü Dafang were chief ministers, Wen Jifu was in mourning in Luoyang, nursing resentment. When his mourning ended he feared he would not win a capital appointment and wrote to Xing Shu: "The appointment should come next month, but whether I can enter court is far from certain. Those in power grow ever more suspicious and resentful of the hawk faction; their following is truly large. Sima Zhao's heart is plain to every passerby. With 'Fen Kun' at their side they surely mean to make me the object of their malice—it is enough to chill the heart. By Sima Zhao he meant Lü Dafang's long tenure as sole holder of power; 'Fen Kun': the age nicknamed imperial sons-in-law 'Fen Marquis'; Han Jiayan had married an imperial princess and called his elder brother Zhongyan 'Fen Kun.' Shu showed the letter to Cai Shuo and Cai Wei. Wei submitted a memorial accusing Zhi, Dafang, and more than a dozen others of framing his father Cai Que and plotting against the dynasty, citing Jifu's letter as evidence. Zhang Dun and Cai Bian were then ceaselessly fabricating charges against the Yuanyou faction; using this affair they sought to execute Zhi, Liang Tao, Wang Yansou, and others. Believing Zhi harbored designs to depose and enthrone, they opened the Tongwen Guan investigation, assigning Cai Jing and An Dun jointly to conduct it, and seized Wen Jifu for questioning. At the end of Yuanyou, Wen Jifu had opposed Dafang's appointment as Acting Vice Minister of the Secretariat; though Zhongyan had been dismissed, Emperor Zhezong's favor had not yet faded. Jifu therefore claimed his late father had once explained that Sima Zhao referred to Liu Zhi: 'Fen' meant Wang Yansou, whose face was white as powder, and 'Kun' meant Liang Tao, courtesy name Kuangzhi—'Kuang' being homophonous with 'elder brother.' Pressed further about the facts, he could only say, "I suspect the affair was of this nature. Just then Zhi died. Cai Jing reported that there was no time for further examination; Zhi's son was stripped of office and the family was exiled to Yingzhou. Over three years ten died of the miasma.
60
徽宗立，詔反其家屬，用子跂請，得歸葬。 跂又伏闕訴及甫之誣，遂貶及甫並渭於湖外，復摯中大夫。 蔡京為相，降朝散大夫。 後又復觀文殿大學士、太中大夫。 紹興初，贈少師，諡曰「忠肅」。
When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, an edict recalled Zhi's family; at the request of his son Qi, the body was permitted burial at home. Qi also prostrated himself at the palace gate to denounce Jifu's false charges; Jifu and Wei were then demoted beyond the lakes, and Zhi's rank of Grand Master of Palace Attendance was restored. When Cai Jing became chief minister, the posthumous rank was reduced to Grand Master for Spreading Dawn. Later his titles of Academician Exemplar of the Hall for Viewing Literary Works and Grand Master of Palace Attendance were restored. At the start of the Shaoxing era he was posthumously honored as Junior Preceptor, with the posthumous name Loyal and Solemn.
61
摯嗜書，自幼至老，未嘗釋卷。 家藏書多自讎校，得善本或手抄錄，孜孜無倦。 少好《禮》學，其究《三禮》，視諸經尤粹。 晚好《春秋》，考諸儒異同，辨其得失，通聖人經意為多。 其教子孫，先行實，後文藝。 每曰：「士當以器識為先，一號為文人，無足觀矣。」
Zhi loved books; from youth to old age he never set a text aside. He personally collated much of his family library; when he found a fine edition he would sometimes copy it by hand, working tirelessly. In youth he loved Ritual studies; his mastery of the Three Rites he regarded as especially refined among the Classics. In later life he turned to the Spring and Autumn Annals, compared the divergences among the Ru scholars, weighed their strengths and weaknesses, and largely penetrated the sage's intent. In instructing his sons and grandchildren, he put character first and literary accomplishment second. He often said, "A scholar should value breadth of mind and judgment above all; once a man is known merely as a man of letters, there is little worth admiring in him."
62
跂能為文章，遭黨事，為官拓落，家居避禍，以壽終。
Qi was a capable writer; caught in the factional persecutions, his official career foundered; he lived at home avoiding further harm and died at an advanced age.
63
蘇頌，字子容，泉州南安人。 父紳，葬潤州丹陽，因徙居之。 第進士，歷宿州觀察推官、知江寧縣。 時建業承李氏後，稅賦圖籍，一皆無藝，每發斂，高下出吏手。 頌因治訊他事，互問民鄰里丁產，識其詳。 及定戶籍，民或自占不悉，頌警之曰：「汝有某丁某產，何不言？ 」民駭懼，皆不敢隱，遂剗剔夙蠹，成賦一邑，簡而易行，諸令視以為法，至領某民拜庭下以謝。 凡民有忿爭，頌喻以鄉黨宜相親善，若以小忿而失歡心，一旦緩急，將何賴焉。 民往往謝去，或半途思其言而止。 時監司王鼎、王綽、楊紘於部吏少許可，及觀頌施設，則曰：「非吾所及也。」
Su Song, whose courtesy name was Zirong, was a native of Nan'an in Quanzhou. His father Shen was buried at Danyang in Runzhou, and the family moved there to settle. He passed the jinshi examination and served successively as Investigating Secretary under the Suzhou observation commission and as magistrate of Jiangning County. Jianye at the time still bore the legacy of the Li dynasty of Southern Tang; tax registers were in complete disorder, and assessments were made entirely at clerks' discretion. While investigating other cases, Song cross-examined people about neighboring households and property, learning the details by heart. When household registers were being compiled, some people failed to declare everything. Song warned them: "You have such-and-such males and such-and-such property—why do you not declare them? Terrified, the people dared conceal nothing. He cut away long-standing abuses and completed tax assessment for the entire county in a simple, workable form. Other magistrates took it as their model, and some community leaders came to bow in thanks at his court. Whenever neighbors quarreled, Song urged them that people of the same community ought to treat one another kindly; if a small grudge destroyed goodwill, whom could they rely on in a crisis? People often went away appeased, or stopped halfway home to reconsider his words and abandon their quarrel. Supervisory commissioners Wang Ding, Wang Chuo, and Yang Hong rarely praised subordinates, but observing Song's work they said, "This is beyond our reach."
64
調南京留守推官，留守歐陽修委以政，曰：「子容處事精審，一經閱覽，則修不復省矣。 」時杜衍老居睢陽，見頌，深器之，曰：「如君，真所謂不可得而親疏者。 」衍又自謂平生人罕見其用心處，遂自小官以至為侍從、宰相所以施設出處，悉以語頌，曰：「以子相知，且知子異日必為此官，老夫非以自矜也。 」故頌後歷政，略似衍云。
He was transferred to investigating secretary under the Nanjing garrison commander. Garrison Commander Ouyang Xiu entrusted him with administrative affairs, saying, "Zirong handles matters with meticulous care; once I have reviewed his work, I need look at it no further. Du Yan was then living in retirement at Suiyang. Meeting Song, he deeply admired him and said, "A man like you is truly what they mean by one who cannot be won by intimacy or alienated by distance. Yan also said that in his lifetime few had seen the full working of his mind. From his days in minor office through his service as court attendant and chief minister—all his principles of action, advancement, and withdrawal—he confided entirely to Song, saying, "Because I know you, and because I know you will one day hold such office, I tell you this—not to boast of myself. Song's later career in government broadly resembled Du Yan's in this respect.
65
皇祐五年，召試館閣校勘，同知太常禮院。 至和中，文彥博為相，請建家廟，事下太常。 頌議以為：「禮，大夫士有田則祭，無田則薦，是有土者乃為廟祭也。 有田則有爵，無土無爵，則子孫無以繼承宗祀，是有廟者止於其躬，子孫無爵，祭乃廢也。 若參合古今之制，依約封爵之令，為之等差，錫以土田，然後廟制可議。 若猶未也，即請考案唐賢寢堂祠饗儀，止用燕器常食而已。」
In the fifth year of Huangyou he was summoned for the library examination as collator and was appointed associate director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. During the Zhehe era, Chief Minister Wen Yanbo petitioned to establish a family temple; the matter was referred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Song argued: "By ritual law, grandees and officers with landholdings sacrifice in temples; without land they offer seasonal presentations—only those with fiefs perform temple worship. Land implies rank; without land and without rank, descendants have no means to maintain ancestral worship—so the right to a family temple ends with the man himself; when descendants hold no rank, sacrifice ceases. Only if institutions past and present are harmonized, enfeoffment edicts are applied with proper gradations, and land is granted accordingly can the question of family temples be seriously entertained. If that cannot be done, then consult the Tang practice of worship in the resting hall, limiting offerings to banquet vessels and ordinary fare."
66
嘉祐中，詔禮院議立故郭皇后神御殿於景靈宮，頌謂：「敕書云：『向因忿鬱，偶失謙恭』，此則無可廢之事。 又云：『朕念其自歷長秋，僅周一紀，逮事先后，祗奉寢園』，此則有不當廢之悔。 又云：『可追復皇后，其祔廟諡冊並停。 』此則有合祔廟及諡冊之義。 請祔郭皇后於后廟，以成追復之道。 」眾論未定，宰相曾公亮問曰：「郭后，上元妃，若祔廟，則事體重矣。 」頌曰：「國朝三聖，賀、尹、潘皆元妃，事體正相類。 今止祔后廟，則豈得有同異之言。 」公亮曰：「議者以謂陰逼母后，是恐萬歲後配祔之意。 」頌曰：「若加一『懷』、『哀』、『愍』之諡，則不為逼矣。 」公亮歎重。
During the Jiayou era, the court ordered the Board of Rites to consider establishing a Spirit Hall for the late Empress Guo at Jingling Palace. Song argued: "The imperial edict reads, 'Previously, in a fit of anger and vexation, I failed in humility'—and that is something that cannot simply be undone. It also says, 'I remember that she held the empress's seat for nearly twelve years, served both the former and the reigning empress, and dutifully tended the imperial tombs'—which shows remorse that her deposition was wrong. It further states, 'She may be posthumously restored as empress, but her enshrinement in the ancestral temple and her posthumous title documents are both suspended. '" That wording still implies the right to temple enshrinement and a posthumous title. I therefore ask that Empress Guo be enshrined in the empresses' temple, so that the restoration may be fully accomplished. " Debate continued without resolution. Chief Minister Zeng Gongliang asked, "Empress Guo was the emperor's consort before he took the throne; enshrining her in the temple would make this a matter of grave consequence. " Song replied, "The Three Sage Emperors of our dynasty—Empresses He, Yin, and Pan—were all primary consorts before enthronement; the precedent is precisely the same. If we enshrine her only in the empresses' temple, as with those precedents, how could anyone argue otherwise? " Gongliang said, "Some argue that this covertly pressures the empress dowager—that it anticipates her eventual enshrinement beside Empress Guo after the emperor's death. " Song said, "If her posthumous title includes a qualifier such as 'Cherished,' 'Lamented,' or 'Pitied,' it would no longer appear coercive. " Gongliang sighed, deeply impressed.

He was transferred to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, where he helped compile and edit the imperial library. Song served at the Hall for nine years, supporting his grandmother and mother and providing for aunts, sisters, and dozens of maternal relatives. The household was warm and well provisioned, and marriages were arranged at the proper times. His wife and children often went without adequate food and clothing, yet he remained entirely unperturbed. Fu Bi had once called Song a gentleman in the ancient mold. When Fu and Han Qi became chief ministers, they jointly recommended his integrity and modesty and appointed him prefect of Yingzhou. Vice-prefect Zhao Zhizhong was a former defector from the frontier who habitually contended with his prefect wherever he served. Song treated him with courtesy and showed him every sincerity. Zhizhong wept and said, "Though I am a frontier man, I yield when I see what is right. In all my life, the only men I have truly admired are you and Duke Han of Wei."
