遷度支判官。 送契丹使，宿恩州，驛舍火，左右請出避，頌不動。 州兵欲入救，閉門不納，徐使防卒撲滅之。 初火時，郡人洶洶，唱使者有變，救兵亦欲因而生事，賴頌安靜而止。 遂聞京師，神宗疑焉。 頌使還，入奏，稱善久之。 命為淮南轉運使。 召修起居注，擢知制誥、知通進銀臺司、知審刑院。
He was transferred to serve as judge in the Revenue Section. While escorting Liao envoys, he lodged at Enzhou. When the relay station caught fire, his attendants urged him to flee, but Song did not stir. When prefectural troops tried to force their way in to rescue him, he shut the door and refused them entry, then calmly had the guards extinguish the blaze. When the fire first broke out, the local populace was in an uproar, claiming the envoys had caused trouble, and the rescue troops were ready to exploit the chaos. Only Song's composure kept matters from escalating. Word reached the capital, and Emperor Shenzong grew suspicious. When Song returned and reported to the throne, the emperor praised him at length. He was appointed transport commissioner for Huainan. He was summoned to compile the imperial diary, then promoted to drafter of edicts and appointed director of both the Gateway Office and the Review Office.

時知金州張仲宣坐枉法贓罪至死，法官援李希輔例，杖脊黥配海島。 頌奏曰：「希輔、仲宣均為枉法，情有輕重。 希輔知台，受賕數百千，額外度僧。 仲宣所部金坑，發檄巡檢體究，其利甚微，土人憚興作，以金八兩屬仲宣，不差官比校，止係違令，可比恐喝條，視希輔有間矣。 」神宗曰：「免杖而黥之，可乎？ 」頌曰：「古者刑不上大夫，仲宣官五品，今貸死而黥之，使與徒隸為伍，雖其人無可矜，所重者，污辱衣冠耳。 」遂免仗黥，流海外，遂為定法。
At the time Zhang Zhongxuan, prefect of Jinzhou, was convicted of corruption in the administration of justice, a capital offense. The judges cited the precedent of Li Xifu and recommended flogging, tattooing, and exile to an island. Song memorialized: "Both Xifu and Zhongxuan perverted the law, but the circumstances differ in severity. Xifu held a censorate post, accepted bribes totaling several hundred thousand cash, and ordained monks beyond the permitted quota. Zhongxuan's district contained a gold mine. He dispatched a patrol inspector to investigate; the yield proved negligible, and the locals feared the disruption of mining. They gave Zhongxuan eight taels of gold. No official was sent to verify the transaction. This was merely a violation of an edict and falls closer to the statute on intimidation—quite different from Xifu's case. " The emperor asked, "What if we exempt the flogging but still tattoo him? " Song replied, "In antiquity, punishment did not extend to grandees. Zhongxuan holds fifth rank. To spare his life yet tattoo him and make him the equal of convict laborers—though the man himself may not deserve sympathy, what matters is the disgrace inflicted on the scholar-official class. " Flogging and tattooing were waived; Zhongxuan was exiled overseas instead, and this became established precedent.

大臣薦秀州判官李定，召見，擢太子中允，除監察御史裏行。 宋敏求知制誥，封還詞頭。 復下，頌當制，頌奏：「祖宗朝，天下初定，故不起孤遠而登顯要者。 真宗以來，雖有幽人異行，亦不至超越資品。 今定不由銓考，擢授朝列； 不緣御史，薦置憲臺。 雖朝廷急於用才，度越常格，然隳紊法制，所益者小，所損者大，未敢具草。 」次至李大臨，亦封還。 神宗曰：「去年詔，臺官有闕，委御史臺奏舉，不拘官職高下。 」頌與大臨對曰：「從前臺官，於太常博士以上、中行員外郎以下舉充。 後為難得資敘相當，故朝廷特開此制。 止是不限博士、員郎，非謂選人亦許奏舉。 若不拘官職高下，並選人在其間，則是秀州判官亦可為裏行，不必更改中允也。 今定改京官，已是優恩，更處之憲臺，先朝以來，未有此比。 幸門一啟，則士塗奔競之人，希望不次之擢，朝廷名器有限，焉得人人滿其意哉！ 」執奏不已，於是並落知制誥，歸工部郎中班，天下謂頌及敏求、大臨為「三舍人」。
Senior ministers recommended Li Ding, vice-prefect of Xiuzhou. He was summoned to audience, promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and appointed investigating censor ad interim. Song Minqiu, who held the post of drafter of edicts, returned the draft commission unsigned. The commission was resubmitted, and it fell to Song to draft the edict. Song memorialized: "In the reigns of our founding emperors, when the realm was newly settled, no one was elevated from obscurity and remoteness to high office. Since Emperor Zhenzong, even men of reclusive or exceptional character have not been promoted beyond their proper rank. Now Li Ding, without passing through the regular examination and appointment process, is promoted to court rank; and without entering through the censorate, is recommended directly to the Censorate. Though the court is eager to employ talent and may exceed ordinary rules, this would wreck established procedure. The gain is small and the damage great. I dare not draft the edict. " When the commission next reached Li Dalin, he returned it as well. Emperor Shenzong said, "Last year's edict authorized the Censorate to recommend candidates for vacant censor posts regardless of rank. " Song and Dalin replied, "Formerly censors were drawn from among officials ranked from Erudite of the Imperial Diener upward down to vice director of the middle rank. Because suitable candidates of matching rank became hard to find, the court specially broadened the rule. The change meant only that the pool was not limited to erudites and directors; it did not authorize recommending men still in the examination track. If rank is ignored and examination-track officials are included, then a Xiuzhou vice-prefect could serve as investigating censor ad interim without even being promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent. Li Ding's promotion to capital official is already an exceptional favor. To place him on the Censorate as well is without precedent since the founding of the dynasty. Once the gate of favor is opened, every ambitious office-seeker will hope for extraordinary promotion. The court's honors are finite—how could everyone be satisfied? " They continued to press their objections until all three were stripped of their posts as drafters of edicts and returned to the rank of director in the Ministry of Works. The realm came to call Song, Minqiu, and Dalin the "Three Academy Draftsmen."

歲餘，知婺州。 方溯桐廬，江水暴迅，舟橫欲覆，母在舟中幾溺矣，頌哀號赴水救之，舟忽自正。 母甫及岸，舟乃覆，人以為純孝所感。 徙亳州，有豪婦罪當杖而病，每旬檢之，未愈，譙簿鄧元孚謂頌子曰：「尊公高明以政稱，豈可為一婦所紿。 但諭醫如法檢，自不誣矣。 」頌曰：「萬事付公議，何容心焉。 若言語輕重，則人有觀望，或致有悔。 」既而婦死，元孚慚曰：「我輩狹小，豈可測公之用心也。 」加集賢院學士、知應天府。 呂惠卿嘗語人曰：「子容，吾鄉里先進，苟一詣我，執政可得也。 」頌聞之，笑而不應。 凡更三赦，大臨還侍從，頌才授秘書監、知通進銀臺司。 吳越飢，選知杭州。 一日，出遇百餘人，哀訴曰：「某以轉運司責逋市易緡錢，夜囚晝繫，雖死無以償。 」頌曰：「吾釋汝，使汝營生，奉衣食之餘，悉以償官，期以歲月而足，可乎？ 」皆謝不敢負，果如期而足。
After a little more than a year, he was appointed prefect of Wuzhou. While traveling upstream at Tonglu, the river suddenly rose in a swift current. The boat heeled and nearly capsized; his mother aboard was nearly drowned. Song cried out and plunged into the water to save her, and the boat suddenly righted itself. His mother had just reached shore when the boat overturned. People took this as a response to his pure filial devotion. Transferred to Bozhou, he encountered a powerful woman liable to flogging who claimed illness. She was examined every ten days but never recovered. Clerk Deng Yuanfu of Qiao told Song's son, "Your father is famed for wise governance—surely he cannot be fooled by one woman. Simply instruct the physician to examine her by the proper procedure, and deception will be impossible. " Song said, "All matters should rest on public deliberation. How could personal intent intrude? If one's words carry too much weight, people will hesitate, and regret may follow. " Before long the woman died. Yuanfu said in shame, "We were petty-minded. How could we fathom the governor's intent? " He was additionally appointed Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Yingtianfu. Lü Huiqing once told others, "Zirong is a senior from my home district. If he would but call on me once, he could become chief minister. " When Song heard this, he smiled and said nothing. After three general amnesties, Dalin returned to court attendance; only then was Song appointed Director of the Archive and director of the Gateway Office. When famine struck Wu and Yue, he was selected as prefect of Hangzhou. One day while out on official business, he encountered more than a hundred people pleading in grief: "We owe the transport office arrears on Market Exchange cash. We are imprisoned by night and bound by day—even death would not settle the debt. " Song said, "I will release you so you can earn a living. After meeting your food and clothing needs, you will repay the state in full over time. Is that acceptable? " All thanked him and pledged not to default, and they repaid the debt exactly on schedule.

頌宴客有美堂，或告將兵欲亂，頌密使捕渠領十輩，荷校付獄中，迨夕會散，坐客不知也。 及修兩朝正史，轉右諫議大夫。 使契丹，遇冬至，其國曆後宋曆一日。 北人問孰為是，頌曰：「曆家算術小異，遲速不同，如亥時節氣交，猶是今夕； 若逾數刻，則屬子時，為明日矣。 或先或後，各從其歷可也。 」北人以為然。 使還以奏，神宗嘉曰：「朕嘗思之，此最難處，卿所對殊善。 」因問其山川、人情向背，對曰：「彼講和日久，頗竊中國典章禮義，以維持其政，上下相安，未有離貳之意。 昔漢武帝自謂：『高皇帝遺朕平城之憂，雖久勤征討，而匈奴終不服。 』至宣帝，呼韓單于稽首稱藩。 唐自中葉以後，河湟陷於吐蕃，憲宗每讀《貞觀政要》，慨然有收復意。 至宣宗時，乃以三關、七州歸於有司。 由此觀之，外國之叛服不常，不繫中國之盛衰也。 」頌意蓋有所諷，神宗然之。
While entertaining guests at the Hall of Beauty, Song received word that garrison soldiers were plotting a revolt. He secretly had ten ringleaders arrested in cangues and sent to prison. By evening the banquet had ended, and the guests knew nothing of it. While compiling the standard histories of the two reigns, he was transferred to Right Remonstrance Adviser. On a mission to the Liao, he encountered the winter solstice, when their calendar lagged the Song calendar by one day. The northerners asked which calendar was correct. Song replied, "Calendar calculations differ slightly in timing. If the solar term arrives during the hai hour, it is still this evening; but if it passes by several quarters, it falls into the zi hour and becomes tomorrow. Whether earlier or later, each side may follow its own calendar. " The northerners accepted this explanation. On returning from his mission he reported to the throne. Emperor Shenzong praised him: "I had considered this problem myself—it is the hardest sort to handle. Your reply was excellent. " He then asked about Liao terrain and the people's loyalties. Song replied, "They have been at peace with us for a long time and have extensively adopted Chinese institutions and ritual to sustain their government. High and low are settled, and there is no sign of disloyalty. Formerly Emperor Wu of Han said, 'High Emperor left me the burden of Pingcheng. Though I campaigned tirelessly for years, the Xiongnu never submitted. ' Yet by the time of Emperor Xuan, Chanyu Huhanye kowtowed and declared himself a vassal. From the mid-Tang onward, the Hehuang region fell to Tibet. Emperor Xianzong, whenever he read the Essentials of Governance from the Zhenguan Era, was stirred with the desire to recover it. By the time of Emperor Xuanzong, the three passes and seven prefectures had been restored to imperial control. From this one sees that foreign submission and rebellion are inconstant and do not depend on China's strength or decline. " Song's meaning clearly carried a subtle admonition, and Emperor Shenzong agreed.

初，頌在開封，國子博士陳世儒妻李惡世儒庶母，欲其死，語群婢曰：「博士一日持喪，當厚餉汝輩。 」既而母為婢所殺，開封治獄，法吏謂李不明言使殺姑，法不至死。 或譖頌欲寬世儒夫婦，帝召頌曰：「此人倫大惡，當窮竟。 」對曰：「事在有司，臣固不敢言寬，亦不敢諭之使重。 」獄久不決。 至是，移之大理。 意頌前次請求，移御史臺逮頌對。 御史曰：「公速自言，毋重困辱。 」頌曰：「誣人死，不可為已，若自誣以獲罪，何傷乎？ 」即手書數百言伏其咎。 帝覽奏牘，以為疑，反覆究實，乃大理丞賈種民增減其文傅致也，由是事得白。 同列猶以嘗因人語及世儒帷薄事，頌應曰：「然。 」以是為泄獄情，罷郡。
Earlier, while Song was at Kaifeng, Li, wife of National University Erudite Chen Shiru, hated her husband's stepmother and wished her dead. She told the maidservants, "When the erudite one day enters mourning, I shall richly reward you. " Before long the stepmother was killed by the maidservants. When Kaifeng tried the case, the law officers held that Li had not explicitly ordered her mother-in-law's murder, and the law did not prescribe death. Some accused Song of seeking leniency for the Shiru couple. The emperor summoned Song and said, "This is a grave violation of human relations and must be thoroughly investigated. " He replied, "The matter rests with the officials in charge. I dare not speak of leniency, nor dare I instruct them to impose heavier punishment. " The case dragged on without resolution. At this point the case was transferred to the Grand Court of Review. Interpreting Song's earlier request as suspicious, the authorities transferred the matter to the Censorate and detained Song for questioning. The censor said, "Sir, confess quickly and spare yourself further hardship and disgrace. " Song said, "I cannot falsely accuse another of a capital crime. If I falsely accuse myself to receive punishment, what harm is there in that? " He immediately wrote out a confession of several hundred characters in his own hand. The emperor reviewed the memorial and found it suspicious. After repeated investigation, it emerged that Grand Court Assistant Jia Zhongmin had altered the text to frame him, and Song was cleared. His colleagues still held it against him that once, when someone mentioned a Confucian scholar's domestic scandal, Song had replied, "Yes." Taking this as a leak of confidential case details, he was dismissed from his prefecture.

未幾，知河陽，改知滄州。 入辭，帝曰：「朕知卿久，然每欲用，輒為事奪，命也夫！ 卿直道，久而自明。 」頌頓首謝。 召判尚書吏部兼詳定官制。 唐制，吏部主文選，兵部主武選； 神宗謂三代、兩漢本無文武之別，議者不知所處。 頌言：「唐制吏部有三銓之法，分品秩而掌選事。 今欲文武一歸吏部，則宜分左右曹掌之，每選更以品秩分治。 」於是吏部始有四選法。
Before long he was appointed prefect of Heyang, then transferred to Cangzhou. When he came to take leave before assuming office, the emperor said, "I have known you for a long time, yet every time I wished to use you, something got in the way. Such is fate! You walk the straight path; in time the truth will make itself plain. " Song kowtowed in thanks. He was summoned to oversee the Ministry of Personnel and to draft reforms to the official system. Under the Tang system, the Ministry of Personnel handled civil appointments and the Ministry of War handled military ones; Emperor Shenzong held that in the Three Dynasties and the Two Han there had originally been no civil-military distinction, and the debaters did not know what to do. Song said, "Under the Tang system the Ministry of Personnel used three selection boards, dividing ranks and grades to manage appointments. If civil and military appointments are now to fall under the Ministry of Personnel, left and right bureaus should manage them, with each selection cycle again divided by rank and grade. With that, the Ministry of Personnel established the four-selection system for the first time.
77
因陛對，神宗謂頌曰：「欲修一書，非卿不可。 契丹通好八十餘年，盟誓、聘使、禮幣、儀式，皆無所考據，但患修書者遷延不早成耳。 然以卿度，此書何時可就？ 」頌曰：「須一二年。 」曰：「果然，非卿不能如是之敏也。 」及書成，帝讀《序引》，喜曰：「正類《序卦》之文。 」賜名《魯衛信錄》。 帝嘗問宗子主祭、承重之義，頌對曰：「古者貴賤不同禮，諸侯、大夫世有爵祿，故有大宗、小宗、主祭、承重之義，則喪服從而異制，匹士庶人亦何預焉。 近代不世爵，宗廟因而不立，尊卑亦無所統，其長子孫與眾子孫無以異也。 今《五服敕》，嫡孫為祖、父為長子猶斬衰三年，生而情禮則一，死而喪服獨異，恐非先王制禮之本意。 世俗之論，乃以三年之喪為承重，不知為承大宗之重也。 臣聞慶曆中，朝廷議百僚應任子者，長子與長孫差優與官，餘皆降殺，亦近古立宗之法。 乞詔禮官、博士參議禮律，合承重者，酌古今收族主祭之禮，立為宗子繼祖者，以異於眾子孫之法。 士庶人不當同用一律，使人知尊祖，不違禮教也。 」除吏部侍郎，遷光祿大夫。 遭母喪，帝遣中貴人唁勞，賜白金千兩。
During an imperial audience, Emperor Shenzong told Song, "I wish to compile a book, and no one but you can do it. Peace with the Khitan has lasted more than eighty years, yet oaths, envoys, ceremonial gifts, and ritual forms all lack documentary support. The only worry is that those compiling the book will delay and not finish it soon. By your estimate, when can this book be finished? " Song said, "One or two years." The emperor said, "Just as I expected. No one but you could be so quick." When the book was finished, the emperor read the preface and said with delight, "It reads just like the Sequence of Hexagrams." It was given the title Records of Faith between Lu and Wei. The emperor once asked about the rites governing lineage heirs who lead sacrifice and bear the ancestral burden. Song replied, "In antiquity noble and base followed different rites. Feudal lords and grandees held hereditary ranks and stipends from generation to generation, so there were major and minor lineages, sacrificial leadership, and the burden of ancestral succession—and mourning garments differed accordingly. What did ordinary scholars and commoners have to do with any of it? In recent times ranks are no longer inherited from generation to generation. Ancestral temples are therefore not established, high and low have no governing order, and eldest sons and grandsons are treated no differently from other descendants. Under the present Five Mourning Grades Edict, a grandson by the principal line mourning a grandfather, and a father mourning an eldest son, still wear three years of the highest mourning grade. In life affection and ritual are the same, yet in death mourning garments alone differ. That may not be what the ancient kings intended when they established the rites. Popular opinion treats the three-year mourning as bearing the ancestral burden, without understanding that it means bearing the burden of the major lineage. I have heard that during the Qingli era, when the court debated officials whose sons were eligible for hereditary appointment, eldest sons and eldest grandsons received slightly preferential offices while the rest were reduced in rank. That too approximates the ancient method of establishing lineages. I beg that Your Majesty summon ritual officials and erudites to deliberate on ritual law. For those who should bear the ancestral burden, weigh the ancient and modern rites of gathering the clan and leading sacrifice, establish them as lineage heirs who succeed the ancestors, and distinguish them from other descendants. Scholars and commoners should not be governed by the same rule, so that people may learn to honor their ancestors and not violate ritual teaching. He was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness. When his mother died, the emperor sent a palace eunuch to offer condolences and granted him one thousand taels of silver.
78
元祐初，拜刑部尚書，遷吏部兼侍讀。 奏：「國朝典章，沿襲唐舊，乞詔史官採《新》、《舊唐書》中君臣所行，日進數事，以備聖覽。 」遂詔經筵官遇非講讀日，進漢、唐故事二條。 頌每進可為規戒、有補時事者，必述己意，反覆言之。 又謂：「人主聰明，不可有所向，有則偏，偏則為患大矣。 今守成之際，應之以無心，則無不治。 」每進讀至弭兵息民，必援引古今，以動人主之意。
At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he was appointed Minister of Justice, then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel while also serving as Lecturer to the Heir Apparent. He memorialized, "Our dynasty's statutes and regulations follow Tang precedent. I beg that Your Majesty order the historiographers to select from the New and Old Books of Tang actions taken by rulers and ministers, and each day submit several items for your review. An edict was then issued that on days when the imperial lecture sessions were not devoted to formal reading, the lecturers should submit two items of Han and Tang precedent. Whenever Song submitted items that could serve as admonitions or bear on current affairs, he always set forth his own views and repeated them at length. He also said, "A ruler is intelligent, but he must not lean in any direction. If he does, he becomes partial, and partiality brings great harm. In a time of preserving what has been achieved, if one responds with an unbiased mind, nothing will go ungoverned. Whenever his submitted readings touched on halting warfare and giving the people rest, he always cited ancient and modern examples to move the ruler's mind.
79
既又請別制渾儀，因命頌提舉。 頌既邃於律曆，以吏部令史韓公廉曉算術，有巧思，奏用之。 授以古法，為臺三層，上設渾儀，中設渾象，下設司辰，貫以一機，激水轉輪，不假人力。 時至刻臨，則司辰出告。 星辰緾度所次，占候則驗，不差晷刻，晝夜晦明，皆可推見，前此未有也。
He then also requested that a new armillary sphere be built, and Song was ordered to take charge of the project. Song was already deeply versed in calendrical astronomy. He found that Han Gonglian, a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, understood calculation and had ingenious ideas, and memorialized that he be employed. Following ancient methods, they built a tower of three tiers: an armillary sphere on top, a celestial globe in the middle, and a time announcer below—all driven by one mechanism, with water turning the wheels and no human labor required. When the hour and quarter arrived, the time announcer came forth to announce it. The positions of the stars along their celestial degrees, when tested by observation, proved accurate to the very moment. Day and night, light and dark, all could be calculated and displayed. Nothing like it had existed before.
80
頌前後掌四選五年，每選人改官，吏求垢瑕，故為稽滯。 頌敕吏曰：「某官緣某事，當會某處，仍引合用條格，具委無漏落狀同上。 」自是吏不得逞。 每訴者至，必取按牘使自省閱，訴者服，乃退； 其不服，頌必往復詰難，度可行行之，苟有疑，則為奏請，或建白都堂。 故選官多感德，其不得所欲者，亦心服而去。
Song oversaw the four selection cycles for five years in all. Whenever candidates sought changes of office, clerks hunted for flaws and deliberately caused delays. Song ordered the clerks, "For such-and-such an office, on account of such-and-such a matter, documents should be assembled at such-and-such a place. Cite the applicable statutes and regulations, and submit a complete report with nothing omitted, together with the memorial." From then on the clerks could not have their way. Whenever a petitioner arrived, he always had the case file brought out for the petitioner to review. If the petitioner was satisfied, he was dismissed; if not satisfied, Song would repeatedly question and challenge the matter. If he judged it feasible he carried it out; if there was doubt he memorialized for decision or raised the matter at the chief council. Many appointees were grateful for his fairness; even those who did not get what they wanted left convinced.
81
遷翰林學士承旨。 五年，擢尚書左丞。 嘗行樞密事。 邊帥遣种樸入奏：「得諜言，阿里骨已死，國人未知所立。 契丹官趙純忠者，謹信可任，願乘其未定，以勁兵數千，擁純忠入其國立之。 」眾議如其請。 頌曰：「事未可知，其越境立君，使彼拒而不納，得無損威重乎？ 徐觀其變，俟其定而撫輯之，未晚也。 」已而阿里骨果無恙。
He was promoted to Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief. In the fifth year he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. He once acted in the affairs of the Bureau of Military Affairs. A frontier commander sent Zhong Pu to report to the throne, "According to spy reports, Aligu is already dead, and the people of the state do not yet know whom they will install. The Khitan official Zhao Chunzhong is prudent and trustworthy and can be entrusted with the task. We wish, while their succession is unsettled, to take several thousand crack troops and escort Chunzhong into their state to install him as ruler. The assembly agreed with his request. Song said, "The matter is still uncertain. If we cross the border to install a ruler and they refuse to accept him, will we not damage our dignity and authority? Watch the situation unfold, wait until it settles and then pacify them—it will not be too late. Before long Aligu proved to be unharmed after all.
82
七年，拜右僕射兼中書門下侍郎。 頌為相，務在奉行故事，使百官守法遵職。 量能授任，杜絕僥倖之原，深戒疆場之臣邀功生事。 論議有未安者，毅然力爭之。 賈易除知蘇州，頌言：「易在御史名敢言，既為監司矣，今因赦令，反下遷為州，不可。 」爭論未決。 諫官楊畏、來之邵謂稽留詔命，頌遂上章辭位，罷為觀文殿大學士、集禧觀使，繼出知揚州。 徒河南，辭不行，告老，以中太一宮使居京口。 紹聖四年，拜太子少師致仕。
In the seventh year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery. As chief minister, Song's aim was to follow established precedent and make all officials observe the law and keep to their duties. He matched ability to appointment, cut off the source of undeserved favor, and sternly warned frontier officials against seeking merit by provoking incidents. When he found something unsettling in deliberation, he resolutely argued against it with all his force. When Jia Yi was appointed prefect of Suzhou, Song said, "Yi was known as outspoken when he served as censor. Now that he has become a supervisory commissioner, to demote him to a prefecture on account of an amnesty is unacceptable. The debate remained unresolved. Remonstrating officials Yang Wei and Lai Zhishao charged that he was delaying imperial edicts. Song thereupon submitted a memorial resigning his post, was removed to serve as Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and Commissioner of Jixi Abbey, and was then sent out as prefect of Yangzhou. He was transferred to Henan but declined to go. He requested retirement on grounds of age and lived at Jingkou as Commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace. In the fourth year of Shaosheng he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and retired from office.
83
方頌執政時，見哲宗年幼，諸臣太紛紜，常曰：「君長，誰任其咎耶？ 」每大臣奏事，但取決於宣仁后，哲宗有言，或無對者。 惟頌奏宣仁后，必再稟哲宗； 有宣諭，必告諸臣以聽聖語。 及貶元祐故臣，御史周秩劾頌。 哲宗曰：「頌知君臣之義，無輕議此老。 」徽宗立，進太子太保，爵累趙郡公。 建中靖國元年夏至，自草遺表，明日卒，年八十二。 詔輟視朝二日，贈司空。
While Song was in power, seeing that Emperor Zhezong was young and the ministers too contentious, he often said, "When the ruler grows up, who will bear the blame? Whenever great ministers reported affairs, decisions were taken only from Empress Dowager Xuanren. When Emperor Zhezong spoke, sometimes no one answered. Only Song, when memorializing Empress Dowager Xuanren, always reported again to Emperor Zhezong; when there was an imperial pronouncement, he always told the ministers to hear the emperor's words. When former Yuanyou ministers were demoted and punished, Censor Zhou Ji impeached Song. Emperor Zhezong said, "Song understands the obligations between ruler and minister. Do not lightly criticize this old man. When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, Song was promoted to Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and his noble rank accumulated to Duke of Zhao Commandery. On the summer solstice of the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo he drafted his own death memorial. The next day he died, at the age of eighty-two. An edict suspended court audiences for two days and posthumously granted him the title of Minister of Works.
84
頌器局閎遠，不與人校短長，以禮法自持。 雖貴，奉養如寒士。 自書契以來，經史、九流、百家之說，至於圖緯、律呂、星官、算法、山經、本草，無所不通。 尤明典故，喜為人言，亹亹不絕。 朝廷有所制作，必就而正焉。
Song's capacity and outlook were broad and far-reaching. He did not measure himself against others in small matters and held himself by ritual and law. Though eminent, he maintained himself like a poor scholar. From the age of written records onward, he mastered the classics and histories, the nine schools, and the teachings of the hundred masters, as well as apocryphal charts, pitch pipes, star offices, calculation methods, mountain classics, and materia medica—there was nothing he did not know. He was especially versed in historical precedents, delighted in speaking to others, and talked on without cease. Whenever the court undertook some new project, it always sought him out to correct and verify it.
85
嘗議學校，欲博士分經； 課試諸生，以行藝為升俊之路。 議貢舉，欲先行實而後文藝，去封彌、謄錄之法，使有司參考其素，行之自州縣始，庶幾復鄉貢里選之遣範，論者韙之。
He once debated school policy, wishing erudites to specialize by classic; students were to be examined and tested, with conduct and talent made the path to advancement. In debating the tribute and selection examinations, he wished character and conduct to come before literary skill. He proposed abolishing sealed copies and transcription, having officials consult a candidate's established record, and beginning the practice at the district and county level—in the hope of restoring the lost model of local recommendation and selection. Commentators approved.
86
論曰：大防重厚，摯骨鯁，頌有德量。 三人者，皆相於母后垂簾聽政之秋，而能使元祐之治，比隆嘉祐，其功豈易致哉！ 大防疏宋家法八事，言非溢美，是為萬世矜式。 摯正邪之辨甚嚴，終以直道慍於群小，遂與大防並死於貶，士論冤之。 頌獨巋然高年，未嘗為奸邪所污，世稱其明哲保身。 然觀其論知州張仲宣受金事，犯顏辨其情罪重輕，又陳刑不上大夫之義，卒免仲宣於黥。 自是宋世命官犯贓抵死者，例不加刑，豈非所為多雅德君子之事，造物者自有以相之歟？
The commentator says: Dafang was grave and solid, Zhi was firm and upright, and Song had moral breadth. All three served as chief ministers during the empress dowager's regency, yet were able to make the Yuanyou governance rise to the level of the Jiayou era. Such achievement is not easily attained! Dafang's memorial on the eight points of the Song house law was no empty praise—it stands as a model for ten thousand generations. Zhi's distinction between upright and corrupt was very strict. In the end, because he walked the straight path he provoked the resentment of petty men, and he died in exile together with Dafang—scholarly opinion held it a grievous wrong. Song alone stood towering in advanced age, never stained by the corrupt, and the world praised him for preserving wisdom and protecting himself. Yet consider his argument in the case of Prefect Zhang Zhongxuan's acceptance of gold: he risked offense to distinguish the gravity of the circumstances and the crime, set forth the principle that punishment does not reach grandees, and in the end spared Zhongxuan from tattooing. From then on, when appointed officials of the Song committed corruption punishable by death, as a rule no physical punishment was applied. Is this not mostly the work of a gentleman of refined virtue—and does not Heaven itself have its way of assisting such men?
